confirmedRules.name: List pagination offset formula
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The ToDo list is returned one page at a time. The number of records skipped is (page - 1) x page size, only non-deleted ToDos count, and the defaults are page size 10 and page 1.
confirmedRules.given: 25 active (non-deleted) ToDos and 3 soft-deleted ToDos in the store
confirmedRules.when: GET /todo?limit=10&page=3 is called
confirmedRules.then: skip = (3 - 1) x 10 = 20, so ToDos #21-#25 come back (5 items). Deleted ToDos are left out before the offset is applied. With no parameters, limit=10 and page=1, so ToDos #1-#10 come back.
confirmedRules.parameters: default limit = 10 (api.py:89, todo_service.py:78, repository.py:92); default page = 1; offset = (page - 1) * limit; filter deleted = false; no upper cap on limit; no ORDER BY clause
edgeCases: page=0 gives skip = -limit, a negative OFFSET. SQLite treats a negative offset as 0, so page 0 returns the same rows as page 1
page=-1 with limit=10 gives skip=-20, which also behaves like page 1 on SQLite
limit=0 returns an empty list (results=0)
limit=-1 means no limit on SQLite, so every active ToDo comes back in one call
limit=10000 is accepted and not capped
There is no ORDER BY, so page contents follow storage order (rowid/insertion order on SQLite). Order is not guaranteed on PostgreSQL/MySQL
Neither the API nor the service validates limit or page. Tests at backend/tests/test_api/test_list_to_do.py:191-290 accept either 200 or 422, which shows the intended behavior was never decided
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: limit and page have no bounds. Negative or zero values quietly fall back to database-specific behavior, and limit=-1 dumps the whole table. With no sort order, pages can overlap or skip items on non-SQLite databases.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What are the valid ranges for page and limit (for example page >= 1, 1 <= limit <= 100)? Should out-of-range values be rejected with 422 or clamped? What sort order should the list use (created_at ascending or descending, title)?

confirmedRules.name: List 'results' count equals items on the current page, not the total
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The 'results' number in the list response is how many ToDos are on this page. It is not the total number of ToDos.
confirmedRules.given: 25 active ToDos
confirmedRules.when: GET /todo?limit=10&page=1 is called
confirmedRules.then: results = 10 (len of the returned page), not 25. For page=3, results = 5.
confirmedRules.parameters: results = len(todo_entries) after invalid rows are skipped
edgeCases: If stored rows fail schema validation and are skipped, results drops below the page size (for example 9 instead of 10)
An empty page gives results=0 and todo_entries=[]. The response schema only rejects null, not an empty list
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Do consumers need a total count (and total pages) for paging? If so, the rewrite needs a separate total field, because the current 'results' is a page count.

confirmedRules.name: Corrupt stored ToDos are silently skipped in list results
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When the list is built, any stored ToDo that fails the output rules (blank title, missing created_at, bad id) is left out of the response and logged as a warning. The request does not fail.
confirmedRules.given: A page of 10 stored ToDos where one row has title '   ' (whitespace only)
confirmedRules.when: GET /todo?limit=10&page=1 is called
confirmedRules.then: 9 ToDos come back with results=9. The bad row is skipped and the log says 'Invalid DB entry skipped'.
confirmedRules.parameters: Output rules: title non-empty after trim; created_at not null; id a valid UUID; empty description becomes null
edgeCases: The skipped row still uses up a slot in the offset/limit window, so the page holds fewer items than limit and the row is never shown on any page
A single-ToDo GET of the same corrupt row is not skipped. ToDoSchema.model_validate raises, which surfaces as a 500 (get_todo endpoint, api.py:53-59)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should corrupt records be hidden quietly, or reported or repaired? Is it acceptable that a list page can hold fewer items than requested?

confirmedRules.name: Delete is a soft delete (record kept, flagged deleted)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Deleting a ToDo only sets its 'deleted' flag to true. The row stays in the database, and deleting a ToDo that is already deleted or does not exist returns 'not found'.
confirmedRules.given: An active ToDo with id 3f2b...-a1 and deleted=false
confirmedRules.when: DELETE /todo/3f2b...-a1 is called twice
confirmedRules.then: The first call sets deleted=true, keeps the row, and returns 200 {success:true, message:'Deleted successfully'}. The second call returns 404 'ToDo not found' because the lookup skips deleted rows.
confirmedRules.parameters: deleted flag default = false; hard_delete_to_do exists in the repository but no API route uses it
edgeCases: Soft-deleted rows stay in the table forever. No purge or retention job exists
A permanent delete (hard_delete_to_do, repository.py:62-68) is implemented but not reachable from the API
There is no undelete or restore path
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is soft delete a business requirement (audit or recovery)? How long should soft-deleted ToDos be kept before permanent purge, and should users be able to restore them?

confirmedRules.name: Soft-deleted ToDos are excluded from every read and update
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Once a ToDo is deleted, it no longer appears in lists, cannot be fetched by id, and cannot be edited or marked done. All of these act as if it does not exist.
confirmedRules.given: A ToDo with id 3f2b...-a1 that has deleted=true
confirmedRules.when: GET /todo/3f2b...-a1, PUT /todo/3f2b...-a1 {title:'X'}, or PUT {done:true} is called
confirmedRules.then: Each call returns 404 'ToDo not found', and GET /todo leaves the item out
confirmedRules.parameters: filter: deleted IS FALSE on get_to_do_entry (lines 88-90), update_to_do (lines 72-74), get_all_to_do_entries (lines 95-97)
edgeCases: Creating a new ToDo with the same id as a soft-deleted one still hits the primary-key conflict and returns 409 'ToDo already exists', even though GET returns 404 for that id
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel split on whether this moves money / is regulatory (Faithful: yes. I read repository.py:70-97 and checked how the service and API use it. All three repository methods filter on `deleted.is_(False)`: update_to_do at lines 72-74, get_to_do_entry at 88-90 and get_all_to_do_entries at 95-97. Each path ends where the card says it does:
- GET /todo/{id}: get_to_do_entry returns None, todo_service.py:49-50 raises ToDoNotFoundError, and api.py:58-59 returns 404 "ToDo not found".
- PUT {title:'X'}: update_to_do returns None, todo_service.py:64-66 raises, and api.py:67-68 returns 404.
- PUT {done:true}: todo_service.py:55-56 sends it to mark_to_do_as_done, which calls get_to_do_entry at 91-93 and raises, giving the same 404.
- GET /todo: the filter is applied before offset/limit at 95-97, so deleted items are left out and do not count toward page sizes.

The id "3f2b...-a1" is a placeholder, not a valid UUID, which is fine for illustration. The same filter has two effects the card leaves out: deleting an already-deleted item returns 404 (delete_to_do line 54), and hard_delete_to_do returns False for soft-deleted rows (line 63). hard_delete is not exposed through the API. Neither point makes the card wrong.

P0 justified: no, under the compliance lens. Nothing here moves money. No regulatory requirement is enforced: a search for audit, retention, GDPR, compliance or regulat finds nothing relevant, and there is no audit trail, retention policy or restore feature. Soft delete actually keeps deleted data in the database, which pulls against erasure obligations rather than meeting them. The data-integrity case is thin. The filter hides tombstoned rows and blocks edits to them, but nothing downstream relies on deleted rows staying unchanged: no restore, audit or reporting. A regulator, auditor or finance controller would not notice if this changed silently.

What would break is the user-facing promise that deleted items stay gone. That is core functional behavior, a strong P1, and the existing tests already cover it (tests/test_api/test_delete_to_do.py and tests/test_service/integration/test_delete_todo_integration.py). The rule could move to P0 only if an SME confirms that deleted records must stay unchanged for a recovery or audit purpose not visible in the code.

The cited lines contain no instruction-like text aimed at automated analysis and no credentials. | The rule is faithful to the code. I traced it myself through repository.py, todo_service.py and api.py, all under <workspace>/legacy/basictodo/backend/app/.

What the code does:
1. All three repository methods filter on `ToDoEntryData.deleted.is_(False)`: update_to_do (repository.py:72-74), get_to_do_entry (repository.py:88-90) and get_all_to_do_entries (repository.py:95-97). The `deleted` column is NOT NULL with default False (database.py:96), so no row can be NULL and the IS FALSE check has no gaps.
2. GET /todo/{id}: get_to_do_entry returns None. The service raises ToDoNotFoundError (todo_service.py:48-50) and the API turns it into 404 "ToDo not found" (api.py:58-59). Matches.
3. PUT {done:true}: the service sends this to mark_to_do_as_done (todo_service.py:55-56). That calls get_to_do_entry, gets None and raises ToDoNotFoundError (todo_service.py:91-93). The decorator passes it through and the API returns 404 (api.py:67-68). Matches.
4. PUT {title:'X'}: 'X' passes the sanitizer and the required-field check. repository.update_to_do then returns None, the service raises ToDoNotFoundError (todo_service.py:64-66), and the API returns 404. Matches.
5. GET /todo: the deleted filter runs before offset/limit, so the item is left out. Matches.

Edge cases the card misses (gaps, not contradictions):
(a) Order of checks on the plain-update path: field validation runs before the not-found check (todo_service.py:59-62). A PUT to a deleted id with an empty title, or one containing an SQL keyword or token, returns 400 "Bad request", not 404. The 404 only appears when the payload passes validation. The `done:true` path skips validation and goes straight to 404.
(b) PUT {done:false} is falsy, so it takes the plain-update path, not the mark-done path. It still returns 404, subject to (a).
(c) DELETE on an already soft-deleted id also returns 404, because delete_to_do calls get_to_do_entry (repository.py:54-56). So deleting twice is not idempotent. hard_delete_to_do also can't reach soft-deleted rows (repository.py:63), but no API route calls it.
(d) Pagination is counted over non-deleted rows only: skip = (page-1)*limit is applied after the filter, so deleted items take up no page slots. The `results` count in the response is the filtered count.
(e) The 404 body is FastAPI's {"detail":"ToDo not found"}.

The card should add (a), (c) and (d) so equivalence tests check them.

P0: justified, but only on data-integrity grounds. Nothing here moves money or meets a regulation. The rule makes "deleted" a final, write-protected state: deleted records can't reappear in reads or be changed by updates. If a rewrite drops this filter, deleted records come back and can be edited. That counts as guarding data integrity.

There is no instruction-like text in the cited lines; the "SQL-injection-safe" docstring at repository.py:39 is an ordinary description. There are no credentials in the cited code.) — confirm criticality.

confirmedRules.name: Marking done takes precedence over other edits in the same update
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If an update request sets done=true, the ToDo is marked complete and any title or description sent in the same request is ignored. The stored title and description are kept.
confirmedRules.given: An active ToDo with title 'Buy milk', description 'Whole', done=false
confirmedRules.when: PUT /todo/{id} with {title:'Buy bread', description:'Rye', done:true}
confirmedRules.then: The response shows title 'Buy milk', description 'Whole', done=true. The new title and description are thrown away without any error.
confirmedRules.parameters: trigger: payload.done is truthy
edgeCases: Marking an already-done ToDo done again works and changes nothing (idempotent)
On the mark-done path the existing title and description are written back without passing through the SQL-keyword sanitizer again
The ToDo must exist and not be deleted, otherwise the result is 404
The frontend has no control to mark a ToDo done (TodoItem.tsx:11-37 renders only Edit and Delete) and does not display done status, so this transition is API-only
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: When done=true is sent together with other fields, the title and description changes are lost and the client is not told.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: When a client marks a ToDo done and edits its text in the same request, should both changes be applied? Is marking done meant to be a user-facing feature (the UI does not offer it today)?

confirmedRules.name: Completed ToDos can be reopened and edited without restriction
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Sending done=false on an update reopens a completed ToDo. Nothing stops a completed ToDo from being reopened or edited.
confirmedRules.given: A ToDo with done=true and title 'File taxes'
confirmedRules.when: PUT /todo/{id} with {done:false}
confirmedRules.then: The normal update path runs, done is set to false, and the ToDo is open again. A later PUT {title:'File taxes 2026'} on a done ToDo also succeeds.
confirmedRules.parameters: status values: done=false (open) and done=true (complete); deleted=true is the terminal state
edgeCases: The lifecycle is open, then done, then open again freely. Any of these states can move to deleted, and deleted is final (no route back)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should completed ToDos be reopenable or editable, or should completion be final or require a separate 'reopen' action?

confirmedRules.name: Partial update changes only the fields supplied
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An update changes only the fields present in the request. Fields left out keep their stored values, and a field explicitly sent as null is set to null.
confirmedRules.given: A ToDo with title 'A' and description 'D'
confirmedRules.when: PUT /todo/{id} with {title:'B'}
confirmedRules.then: The title becomes 'B' and the description stays 'D'. PUT {description:null} clears the description, and the API returns it as null.
confirmedRules.parameters: model_dump(exclude_unset=True); updatable fields: title, description, done
edgeCases: PUT {} with an empty body changes nothing and returns the current ToDo, or 404 if it is missing or deleted

PUT {title:null} skips title validation (service only validates when title is not None), then tries to store a NULL title against a NOT NULL column. That raises an IntegrityError, which is mapped to ToDoAlreadyExistsError, which the update endpoint does not catch, so the client gets a 500
Title and description values go through the sanitizer and trim first (see the sanitizer and required-title rules)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Sending an explicit null title gives an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 validation error.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should an explicit null title be rejected with 400 'title is required'? Should clients be allowed to clear the description by sending null?

confirmedRules.name: Title is required and cannot be blank
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every ToDo needs a title that is not empty after leading and trailing spaces are removed, both when it is created and when its title is changed.
confirmedRules.given: A user submits a ToDo
confirmedRules.when: the title is '   ' (spaces only)
confirmedRules.then: Create: the request schema rejects it with 422 ('title must not be null.'). Update: the service rejects it with 400 'Bad request' (internally 'Invalid payload: title is required'). Frontend: 'Todo title cannot be empty' is shown and nothing is sent.
confirmedRules.parameters: blank = empty after strip()
edgeCases: The same blank title gets different HTTP codes: 422 on create (Pydantic request validation) and 400 on update (service validation)
A missing title on create returns 422
The frontend edit form disables Save while an error is displayed (TodoEditForm.tsx:96-102)

confirmedRules.name: Title and description limited to 255 characters
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Titles and descriptions may be at most 255 characters. The UI blocks longer input, but the backend relies only on a database CHECK constraint, and a violation comes back as a misleading 'already exists' error.
confirmedRules.given: An API client (not the UI) sends a title of 300 characters
confirmedRules.when: POST /todo is called
confirmedRules.then: No API-level check runs. The DB CHECK 'length(title) <= 255' fails at commit with an IntegrityError, which is mapped to ToDoAlreadyExistsError and returned as 409 'ToDo already exists'. In the UI, the input's maxLength=255 stops typing at 255 characters, and the trimmed-length check (> 255) is a second guard.
confirmedRules.parameters: MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 255 (frontend, both forms); CHECK title_length_check length(title) <= 255; CHECK description_length_check length(description) <= 255; String(255) columns
edgeCases: The same overflow on PUT raises ToDoAlreadyExistsError, which the update endpoint does not catch, so the client gets a 500

The CHECK constraints exist only on the ToDoORM DDL model (Base.metadata, created by main.py and init_db.py). The imperative mapping used for reads and writes (database.py:89-100) declares no constraints. If the schema was created any other way, nothing enforces the limit, because SQLite ignores VARCHAR length
The frontend sends a fixed description, so the description limit can only be reached through the API
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Overlong text returns 409 'ToDo already exists' on create and 500 on update, instead of a 400/422 validation error. The limit depends on how the database schema was created.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is 255 characters the real business limit for both title and description? Should the API check it explicitly and return a clear validation error?

confirmedRules.name: SQL keyword and character blocklist on all text input
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Any title or description containing certain punctuation (;, --, /*, */) or certain whole words, matched without regard to case (including everyday words like 'or', 'create', 'update', 'delete', 'select', 'drop'), is rejected as a suspected SQL injection.
confirmedRules.given: A user creates a ToDo with title 'Buy milk or bread'
confirmedRules.when: POST /todo is called
confirmedRules.then: The request is rejected with 400 'Bad request' because the whole word 'or' matches. 'Update resume', 'Create slides', 'Drop off kids', 'Select a gift', and 'Eggs; milk' are rejected too. 'This was updated yesterday' and 'ORDERED pizza' are accepted because the keyword must be a whole word.
confirmedRules.parameters: Case-insensitive regex. Blocked tokens anywhere in the text: '--', ';', '/*', '*/'. Blocked whole words: xp_cmdshell, drop, delete, insert, update, exec, execute, union, select, shutdown, create, alter, rename, truncate, declare, or
edgeCases: The check runs on the raw value, before trimming. The trimmed value is returned
A null value passes through as null, and the optional description becomes ''
Non-string values are turned into strings ('123', 'True') and logged as a warning
Single and double quotes, newlines, tabs, unicode, and emoji are allowed
The same check applies to description on create and update, but not on the mark-done path
The frontend has no matching check, so users only see a generic 'API Error 400: Bad request' toast
Tests (backend/tests/test_data/constants.py:6-52) pin this behavior, including rejecting '1=1 OR 1=1'
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The blocklist rejects ordinary English task titles (any use of 'or', 'create', 'update', 'delete', 'select', 'drop', 'rename', 'alter', or a semicolon). Data access already uses parameterized ORM queries (repository.py), so the filter adds no injection protection and causes many false rejections.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the rewrite keep this keyword blocklist, given that it rejects common task wording? Or can it be dropped in favor of parameterized queries, keeping only explicit length and format rules?

confirmedRules.name: Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed from text fields
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Titles and descriptions are stored and returned without leading or trailing spaces. Spaces, tabs, and line breaks inside the text are kept.
confirmedRules.given: A title of '  Wash dishes  ' and a description of '  Read to p.223  '
confirmedRules.when: the ToDo is created or updated
confirmedRules.then: They are stored and returned as 'Wash dishes' and 'Read to p.223'. 'Line1\nLine2' is kept as is.
confirmedRules.parameters: Python str.strip() / JS String.trim()
edgeCases: Whitespace-only text trims to '', which fails the required-title rule. For description, '' is returned as null

confirmedRules.name: Empty description is stored as blank and returned as null
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Description is optional. If it is missing or blank it is saved as an empty string, and the API always shows it as null.
confirmedRules.given: POST /todo with id and title 'Wash dishes' and no description
confirmedRules.when: the ToDo is created
confirmedRules.then: The stored description is '' (not NULL), and the response shows description: null
confirmedRules.parameters: validate_optional returns '' when the sanitized value is None or empty; the output schema maps any falsy description to None
edgeCases: A description of '   ' becomes '' when stored and null in the response
On update, an explicit {description:null} skips validation and stores NULL, which is also returned as null. Stored values can therefore be '' or NULL while the API shows null for both

confirmedRules.name: ToDo id is a client-supplied UUID and must be unique
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The client creates the ToDo's identifier (a UUID) and sends it. A create request without a valid UUID is rejected, and reusing an existing id is reported as a conflict.
confirmedRules.given: A ToDo with id 7c1e...-09 already exists
confirmedRules.when: POST /todo with id 7c1e...-09 and title 'Another'
confirmedRules.then: The primary-key violation raises an IntegrityError, which is returned as 409 'ToDo already exists'. A missing or non-UUID id returns 422 from request validation.
confirmedRules.parameters: id type UUID (frontend generates uuid v4); primary key on id
edgeCases: The id is still taken after a soft delete, so recreating it returns 409
Every IntegrityError on create (including the 255-character CHECK violation) is reported as 409 'already exists', not only duplicate ids
GET, PUT, and DELETE path ids must parse as UUIDs or FastAPI returns 422 before the service runs (api.py:53-54,62-63,75-76; uuid_validator.py:16-24)
The server never generates an id. The ORM's default=uuid.uuid4 is never used because the builder requires payload.id
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the server generate ToDo ids instead of trusting client-supplied UUIDs? Should a duplicate id be told apart from other integrity failures?

confirmedRules.name: New ToDo initial state and creation timestamp
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every new ToDo starts open (not done), not deleted, with no update time, and its creation time is the server's current local time.
confirmedRules.given: POST /todo with id 7c1e...-09 and title 'Wash dishes' on a server running in UTC+2 at 2026-10-03 14:05:00 local time
confirmedRules.when: the ToDo is created
confirmedRules.then: created_at = 2026-10-03T14:05:00 (naive local time, no timezone offset), updated_at = null, done = false, deleted = false
confirmedRules.parameters: done=false; deleted=false; updated_at=None; created_at=datetime.datetime.now() (naive, server local time)
edgeCases: created_at is naive local time saved in a TIMESTAMP(timezone=True) column, so the timezone is lost and moving servers or changing DST shifts how it reads
The DDL-only model ToDoORM has default=datetime.datetime.now() evaluated once at import (database.py:74), a frozen timestamp. It is never used for inserts because the builder always sets created_at

The imperative table gives updated_at a default of func.now() (database.py:96). Depending on how SQLAlchemy treats an explicit None, the stored updated_at may be the insert time rather than NULL, while the create response shows null
Client-supplied done or deleted values cannot be set at creation because the create schema has no such fields
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should created_at be stored in UTC with a timezone? Should a newly created ToDo have updated_at null or equal to created_at?

confirmedRules.name: Last-updated timestamp is never maintained on change
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Editing, completing, or deleting a ToDo does not change its updated_at value on the server, even though the UI briefly shows the current time as the update time.
confirmedRules.given: A ToDo created at 2026-10-01 09:00 with updated_at null
confirmedRules.when: PUT /todo/{id} {title:'New'} is called on 2026-10-03 14:05
confirmedRules.then: The server leaves updated_at unchanged (null). The frontend shows updated_at=now right away (optimistic), then the refetch replaces it with the server value.
confirmedRules.parameters: No server code assigns updated_at on update, mark-done, or soft delete
edgeCases: The update schema has no updated_at field and the repository only copies fields that were sent
The DB-level default func.now() applies only on insert, not on update (no onupdate defined)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: updated_at exists in the schema and the API contract but is never set when a ToDo is modified, so any audit or 'recently changed' feature built on it would get wrong data.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should updated_at be set to the current time on every edit, completion, and delete? Is any report or sort order expected to rely on it?

confirmedRules.name: Characters-remaining counter shown near the title limit
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: While typing a title, the user sees how many characters are left once fewer than 50 of the 255 remain.
confirmedRules.given: A user has typed a 210-character title
confirmedRules.when: the form re-renders
confirmedRules.then: remaining = 255 - 210 = 45, so '45 characters remaining' is shown. At 205 characters remaining = 50 and nothing is shown, because the threshold is strictly less than 50.
confirmedRules.parameters: MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 255; near-limit threshold: remaining < 50 (title length >= 206); hidden when the field is empty or an error is displayed
edgeCases: The counter uses the raw, untrimmed length, but validation uses the trimmed length, so padding spaces count against the counter but not against the limit
Input maxLength=255 means remaining never goes below 0 through typing

confirmedRules.name: UI overwrites description with a fixed placeholder
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The web UI has no description field. Every ToDo it creates gets the description 'not implemented yet', and every edit through the UI resets the description to that text.
confirmedRules.given: A ToDo whose description was set to 'Read to page 223' through the API
confirmedRules.when: the user edits only its title in the UI
confirmedRules.then: PUT sends {title:'<new>', description:'not implemented yet'}, and the real description is lost
confirmedRules.parameters: description literal = 'not implemented yet'
edgeCases: The UI never displays description, done, created_at, or updated_at (TodoItem.tsx:11-37, TodoList.tsx:37-43)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: UI edits silently destroy descriptions entered through the API, and placeholder text ends up in production data.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should descriptions be editable in the new UI? Should existing 'not implemented yet' values be migrated to null?

confirmedRules.name: UI only ever shows the first 10 ToDos
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The main screen always asks for page 1 with 10 items and has no paging control, so users cannot see their 11th ToDo or later ones.
confirmedRules.given: A user has 12 active ToDos
confirmedRules.when: the main list loads
confirmedRules.then: Only the first 10 in server storage order appear. ToDos #11 and #12 cannot be reached in the UI.
confirmedRules.parameters: limit = 10, page = 1 (hardcoded in TodoList and in the optimistic-cache keys of all mutation hooks)
edgeCases: A newly created 11th ToDo appears at the top for a moment (optimistic prepend), then disappears after the refetch because the server puts it past position 10
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: ToDos beyond the first 10 are hidden from users with no way to reach them.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What page size and paging style (pages, infinite scroll, show all) should the new UI use?

confirmedRules.name: Optimistic list adjustments on create, update and delete
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The screen updates right away, before the server answers: a new ToDo goes to the top and the count goes up by 1, a deleted ToDo is removed and the count goes down by 1, and an edited ToDo shows the new values with the current time. On failure the previous list is restored, and the list is always refetched afterwards.
confirmedRules.given: The cached list shows results=4 with 4 ToDos
confirmedRules.when: the user creates 'Call mom'
confirmedRules.then: The cache immediately shows 'Call mom' first, with results=5, done=false, created_at=now. If the server rejects it, the cache goes back to the 4-item list, and in every case the list is refetched.
confirmedRules.parameters: create: results + 1, prepend; delete: results - 1, filter by id; update: merge fields and set updated_at = now; rollback to snapshot on error; invalidate ['todos'] when settled
edgeCases: Optimistic order (newest first) differs from server order (storage order), so items jump after the refetch
Only the limit=10/page=1 cache entry is adjusted
The optimistic description is null when not supplied, but the UI always supplies 'not implemented yet'

confirmedRules.name: Delete requires confirmation; success message shown before server confirms
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Before deleting, the user must confirm 'Do you really want to delete this item?'. The 'Todo deleted' success message then appears straight away, before the server has confirmed.
confirmedRules.given: A user clicks 'Delete Todo' and confirms the dialog
confirmedRules.when: the server call fails (for example 404 or 500)
confirmedRules.then: The user sees 'Todo deleted' (success) first, then 'Failed to delete todo' with a Retry button, and the item comes back in the list

1. Deleting only sets a flag; the row is never removed. delete_to_do first looks the todo up with get_to_do_entry, which only matches id=X AND deleted IS FALSE (repository.py:88-90). If nothing comes back it returns False, the service raises ToDoNotFoundError, and the API returns 404 with detail "ToDo not found". Otherwise it sets entry.deleted = True on the object it just read (no longer attached to a session) and calls session.merge (repository.py:57-59). safe_session_scope then commits (database.py:54-64; expire_on_commit=False at database.py:51). Nothing calls session.delete. hard_delete_to_do (repository.py:62-68) exists but is never called from the service or the API.

2. The done flag is not touched, so the claim "done unchanged" holds.

3. A successful delete returns HTTP 200, FastAPI's default, with success=true and message="Deleted successfully" (api.py:79).

4. A second DELETE on the same id returns 404, because the lookup filters out deleted rows. The parameter citation repository.py:89 is correct (the filter spans 88-90).

Minor gaps that don't make the card wrong but should go into the behavior contract:
(a) The full response body is {success:true, data:null, message:"Deleted successfully", error:null}. DeleteToDoResponse inherits data and error from ApiResponse (api_response.py:8-12), so the card's body is only part of what is sent.
(b) "done unchanged" really means done keeps the value read at lookup time. merge copies every loaded attribute from that snapshot, so if done/title/description change between the lookup and the merge, the delete overwrites the newer values (a race where the later write is lost).
(c) updated_at is not changed either.
(d) An id that never existed also returns 404. A malformed id returns 422 from FastAPI's UUID path parsing, so the 400 branch at api.py:82-83 can't be reached over HTTP.
(e) Clients supply the todo's id (create_todo_schema.py:9; todo_entry_builder.py:27), and the deleted row keeps its primary key. So trying to create a new todo with a deleted todo's id hits an IntegrityError, which the API turns into 409 "ToDo already exists" (decorators.py:31-32, api.py:45-46). That is behavior users can see.

P0 rating: this rule doesn't move money or enforce a regulation. It still counts as data integrity and retention. Deleted records must stay in the database and must not show up in any read (get, update and list all filter on deleted IS FALSE at repository.py:73, 89 and 96). A rewrite that switched to real deletes would lose data permanently and would also start allowing deleted ids to be reused, which changes behavior clients can see.

The API tests (backend/tests/test_api/test_delete_to_do.py) mock the service, so the database behavior is not tested anywhere. The cited lines contain no instruction-like text and no credentials.) — confirm criticality.

confirmedRules.parameters: Messages: 'ToDo already exists', 'Bad request', 'Internal error', 'ToDo not found'

confirmedRules.name: New ToDo's last-updated timestamp is filled by the database clock (UTC) at insert, not left empty
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The code tries to create a ToDo with no last-updated time, but the database fills that field with its own current time (UTC, whole seconds) when the row is saved. The creation time comes from the server's local clock, so on a server that isn't on UTC the 'last updated' time can be earlier than the 'created' time.
confirmedRules.given: A backend server running at local time UTC+2 (CEST), using the default SQLite store
confirmedRules.when: A client POSTs /todo {"id":"<new uuid>","title":"Buy milk"} at 2026-10-03 14:00:00.123456 server-local time
confirmedRules.then: created_at is stored as 2026-10-03T14:00:00.123456 (server-local, no timezone, from datetime.now()). updated_at is stored as 2026-10-03T12:00:00 (SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, UTC, whole seconds). The builder sets updated_at=None, but the ORM leaves None values out of the INSERT for columns that have a default, so to_do_table's default=func.now() is applied instead. On SQLite 3.35 or later the value is read back with RETURNING, so the create response and later GETs show a non-null updated_at that is 2 h earlier than created_at.
confirmedRules.parameters: updated_at column default = func.now() (database.py:96); created_at default = func.now() (database.py:95, never used because the builder always supplies it); created_at value = datetime.datetime.now() server-local (todo_entry_builder.py:30); legacy declarative ToDoORM created_at default = datetime.datetime.now() evaluated once at import (database.py:74); SQLAlchemy 2.0.43 (uv.lock:777-778)
edgeCases: UTC server: updated_at roughly equals created_at but is cut to whole seconds, so it can look up to <1 s earlier than created_at
PostgreSQL/MySQL DATABASE_URL (allowed by database.py:33): now() gives the database's own transaction time with that server's timezone handling, so the result depends on the backend

confirmedRules.given: 3 active ToDos
confirmedRules.when: GET /todo?limit=10&page=2
confirmedRules.then: The response is 200 {"success": true, "results": 0, "todo_entries": []}. The UI shows 'No todos yet. Add one above!' when page 1 is empty.
confirmedRules.parameters: results default = 0 (get_list_to_do_response.py:13); validator rejects only None (line 19)
edgeCases: Test comments say 'empty lists are rejected by schema' (test_list_to_do.py:16, 293), but the validator only rejects None, so the comment is wrong

confirmedRules.name: Duplicate ToDo titles are permitted
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Two ToDos can have exactly the same title. Only the id has to be unique.
confirmedRules.given: An active ToDo titled "Buy milk" exists
confirmedRules.when: A client POSTs /todo with a new id and title "Buy milk"
confirmedRules.then: The ToDo is created with 200 and the list now has two "Buy milk" entries. The title column has an ordinary (non-unique) index, and the only conflict check is the primary-key id.
confirmedRules.parameters: title column: String(255), nullable=False, index=True, no unique constraint
edgeCases: The same title is also allowed after case or whitespace changes, since there is no normalization-based uniqueness
Any IntegrityError on create (e.g. a CHECK constraint) is reported as 'ToDo already exists' (already catalogued), but title duplication never triggers one

confirmedRules.name: Any UUID version, including the all-zero (nil) UUID, is accepted as a ToDo id
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The server only checks that the id parses as a UUID. It does not check the version or reject the all-zero id, and alternative spellings are converted to the standard hyphenated form.
confirmedRules.given: No ToDo with the nil id exists
confirmedRules.then: The ToDo is created. The 'if not value' check never fires because Python UUID objects are always truthy, and there is no version check. A second POST with the same nil id gets 409.
confirmedRules.parameters: Id type: uuid.UUID, any version (not UUID4)
edgeCases: A 32-hex-digit id without hyphens, or a braced/urn form, is accepted (depending on the Pydantic parser) and returned in canonical hyphenated form
The UI always generates v4 ids (TodoForm.tsx:49), so this only matters for direct API clients
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the server accept only randomly generated (v4) ids and reject the nil UUID and non-canonical spellings, or is any parseable UUID acceptable?

confirmedRules.name: Any caller may read, edit, complete or delete any todo (no ownership or authorization check)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: There are no users and no owners: every todo sits in one shared list, and any request that reaches the API can view, change, mark done or delete any todo. The only restriction is a browser-origin (CORS) allow-list.
confirmedRules.given: One backend shared by Alice and Bob. Alice created todo id 3f2b9c1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 titled 'Pay rent'.
confirmedRules.when: Bob sends DELETE /todo/3f2b9c1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 (or PUT with {"done": true}) without any credentials
confirmedRules.then: The response is HTTP 200 {success: true, message: 'Deleted successfully'}. Alice's todo disappears from every list. No identity is checked, and no actor is recorded on the record.
confirmedRules.parameters: Allowed browser origin = http://localhost:5173 (credentials allowed, all methods and headers); no auth scheme or dependency on any endpoint; the data model has no owner/user field (id, title, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted, done only)
edgeCases: CORS only limits browsers on other origins. curl, scripts and server-to-server callers are not restricted at all.
GET /todo lists every active id, so ids do not need to be guessed before deleting or editing someone else's todo.
The e2e suite relies on this: it bulk-deletes every todo through unauthenticated calls (frontend/e2e/todo-validation.spec.ts:6-15).
README.md:3 says the app is a playground 'not intended for production usage'. This is consistent with deliberately having no auth.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is the todo list meant to stay one shared list with no user accounts, or must the rewrite add per-user ownership so that only the creator can view, edit, complete or delete a todo?

confirmedRules.name: Server rejections reach the user as a generic status message with no reason
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When the server rejects a create, edit or delete, the user only sees 'API Error <status>: <generic detail>'. The specific reason the service worked out (for example, which forbidden word was found) is thrown away.
confirmedRules.given: A user types the title 'Buy milk or bread'. It passes the browser checks: not blank and at most 255 characters.
confirmedRules.when: The user presses Enter to create the todo
confirmedRules.then: The server's blocklist rejects the word 'or' and returns HTTP 400 {"detail": "Bad request"}. A toast appears with title 'Failed to create todo', text 'API Error 400: Bad request' and a Retry button. Nothing is created, and pressing Retry gets the same rejection.
confirmedRules.parameters: Detail strings: 409 'ToDo already exists', 400 'Bad request', 404 'ToDo not found', 500 'Internal error'. Message format: 'API Error {status}: {detail || statusText}'. Toast default duration 5000 ms, placement bottom-end.
edgeCases: FastAPI 422 schema errors return 'detail' as a list of objects, so the message shows 'API Error 422: [object Object]'. The UI's own checks make this hard to reach.

Unhandled server errors (for example GET of a corrupt record, or any list-endpoint failure) return plain text, not JSON. The message then falls back to the status text, 'API Error 500: Internal Server Error'.
A todo deleted elsewhere while being edited gives 'API Error 404: ToDo not found'. The list then refetches and the item disappears.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The service builds a specific reason ('Invalid characters or SQL keywords in input: ...' at input_sanitizer.py:39, 'Invalid payload: title is required' at field_validator.py:34). The API replaces it with the fixed text 'Bad request' (api.py:48,70,83), so users cannot tell which word or field caused the rejection.

confirmedRules.name: A failed create or edit keeps the user's input and offers a Retry that resends the identical request
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The input is cleared (create) or the edit form closed (edit) only after the server confirms success. On failure the text stays and a Retry button resends exactly the same request, including the same client-generated todo id.
confirmedRules.given: A user types 'Buy groceries'. The browser generates id 7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7. The server responds with HTTP 500.
confirmedRules.when: The user presses Enter
confirmedRules.then: The request is automatically resent once (mutation retry = 1). If it still fails, a 'Failed to create todo' toast with Retry appears and 'Buy groceries' stays in the input. Clicking Retry posts the same id 7c9e6679-... and the same title. Only on success is the input cleared and the 'Todo created' toast shown. For edits, the edit form stays open on failure and closes only on success.
confirmedRules.parameters: mutations.retry = 1; queries.retry = 1; Retry action label 'Retry'; create input disabled while a create is in flight
edgeCases: If the first POST was saved but its response was lost, the automatic or manual retry gets 409 'ToDo already exists'. The user sees a failure toast even though the todo exists, and the list refetch then shows it.
If the user presses Enter again instead of clicking Retry, handleSubmit generates a new UUID. When the first attempt had actually been saved, this creates a second todo with the same title.
Business rejections (400 blocklist, 409 duplicate) are also automatically resent once before the error toast. Each click on Retry sends up to two more identical requests.
The create input is disabled while a create is pending (TodoForm.tsx:87), which blocks double-submission during a single attempt.

confirmedRules.name: Any syntactically valid UUID is accepted as a todo id, including the all-zero UUID and alternate spellings
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The id check only asks 'does this parse as a UUID'. It does not check the version and does not reject the nil (all-zero) UUID, and differently written forms of the same UUID are treated as the same id.
confirmedRules.given: An empty todo store
confirmedRules.when: A client sends POST /todo {"id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000", "title": "Test"}, then POST /todo {"id": "6F9619FF8B86D011B42D00C04FC964FF", "title": "A"}, then POST /todo {"id": "6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00c04fc964ff", "title": "B"}
confirmedRules.then: The first call returns 200 and creates a todo with the nil id. The second returns 200 and the id comes back as '6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00c04fc964ff'. The third returns 409 'ToDo already exists', because it is the same UUID written differently.
confirmedRules.parameters: No UUID version check (v1/v3/v4/v5/nil all accepted). Accepted text forms depend on the pydantic UUID parser: hyphenated, 32-hex, upper or lower case.
edgeCases: A missing or null id is rejected by the field type with 422 before the 'must not be null' validator runs.
Path ids on GET/PUT/DELETE go through the same parser, so a nil-UUID todo can be read, edited and deleted like any other.
The service's UUIDValidator (400 on failure) is unreachable from the HTTP API, because FastAPI already rejects malformed path ids with 422.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The 'id must not be null' guards (create_todo_schema.py:16-17, todo_schema.py:54-55) can never fire: UUID objects are always truthy (checked in Python), and a null id is already rejected by the type. Re-parsing at create_todo_schema.py:18-21 and todo_schema.py:56-59 is redundant. As a result the nil UUID is accepted as a real identifier.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the rewrite accept only randomly generated version-4 UUIDs (rejecting the nil UUID and other versions), or should id generation move to the server?

confirmedRules.name: Editing can clear a todo's description (null or blank), unlike the title
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: On update, the description can be removed by sending null or blank text. Null skips all checks and is stored as an empty database value. Blank text is trimmed to an empty string. Both are returned as 'no description'.
confirmedRules.given: An active todo 'Call plumber' with description 'Before 5pm'
confirmedRules.when: A client sends PUT /todo/{id} with {"description": null}, or with {"description": "   "}
confirmedRules.then: Both return HTTP 200 with description: null and the title unchanged. The null request stores database NULL and bypasses the blocklist. The blank request stores an empty string. Sending {"description": "select tiles"} instead returns 400 because of the blocklisted keyword.
confirmedRules.parameters: description column nullable = true (String 255)
edgeCases: There are two physical forms of 'no description': empty string (from create or a blank edit) and NULL (from an explicit null edit). Both read back as null.
The web UI cannot clear a description, because it always sends the placeholder 'not implemented yet'. Clearing is possible only through the API.
Contrast: an explicit null title or done in the same request causes a server error. Only description supports clearing.

confirmedRules.name: API response envelope: success flag plus payload on success, bare detail on failure
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every successful call returns success = true with the todo, or a 'Deleted successfully' message, and HTTP 200, including for create. Every failure returns only {"detail": "..."}. The envelope's success = false and error fields are never used.
confirmedRules.given: A valid new todo {id: 'a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001', title: 'Wash dishes'}
confirmedRules.when: The client POSTs it, later DELETEs it, then DELETEs it again
confirmedRules.then: The create returns HTTP 200 (not 201) with {success: true, data: null, message: null, error: null, todo_entry: {...}}. The first delete returns 200 with {success: true, message: 'Deleted successfully', data: null, error: null}. The second delete returns 404 with {detail: 'ToDo not found'}, with no success field.
confirmedRules.parameters: Create success status = 200; delete success message = 'Deleted successfully'; single-todo responses require todo_entry to be present
edgeCases: Single-todo responses declare todo_entry as required, so a missing todo is rejected by the type. The extra 'must not be null' validator never adds anything, because pydantic model instances are always truthy.
The frontend only reads detail from failures (types/todo.ts:76-78) and never checks success = false.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: ApiResponse defines error, data and success = false (api_response.py:9-12), but no endpoint ever fills them. Clients built against the documented envelope would expect failures in that shape and find {detail} instead.

confirmedRules.name: New todos must start not-deleted, but the model's default for 'deleted' is not a boolean (masked by the builder)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A todo is meant to be active (not deleted) until someone deletes it. Today that holds only because the single creation path always passes deleted = false. The domain model's own default for 'deleted' is a database column-definition object, not false.
confirmedRules.given: Code that builds a todo record without passing the deleted flag, such as a future import, migration or alternative creation path
confirmedRules.when: The record is constructed and saved
confirmedRules.then: Its deleted attribute holds a SQLAlchemy mapped-column object (truthy, not a boolean) instead of false. Insert probably fails or the record is treated as deleted. In current code every construction (builder and all test factories) passes deleted=False explicitly, so API-created todos start with deleted = false and done = false.
confirmedRules.parameters: Model default deleted = mapped_column(default=False) (column object); model default done = False; table default deleted = False
edgeCases: The database table default deleted = False (database.py:97) applies only when the column is left out of the INSERT. The ORM sends the attribute value, so the table default does not rescue a bad model default.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: models/todo.py:17 sets `deleted: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(default=False, name='deleted')` as a dataclass field default. The generated constructor uses the column object itself as the default value, not False.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is there any creation path other than POST /todo (bulk import, data migration, admin script) that must create todos? If so, confirm they must always start with deleted = false and done = false regardless of how they are constructed.

confirmedRules.name: A todo being edited cannot be deleted from the UI, and Cancel discards changes without asking
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: While a todo is in edit mode, its Edit and Delete buttons are hidden. The edit box starts with the current title, and Cancel throws away unsaved changes with no confirmation.
confirmedRules.given: The list shows the todo 'Original todo'
confirmedRules.when: The user clicks Edit, types 'Changed text', then clicks Cancel
confirmedRules.then: While editing, the 'Edit' and 'Delete Todo' buttons for that item are hidden. Clicking Cancel closes the form immediately with no prompt, and the item still reads 'Original todo'. A successful Save also closes the form.
confirmedRules.parameters: none
edgeCases: This is a UI-only guard. The server does not lock a todo while it is being edited, and anyone can delete it through the API meanwhile. A later Save then gets 404 'ToDo not found'.
Each item has its own edit state, so several todos can be in edit mode at once.

confirmedRules.name: The done flag has no state guard: marking a done todo done again, or reopening an open todo, succeeds silently
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Marking a todo done never checks its current status. Asking to mark an already-done todo done, or to reopen a todo that is already open, returns success with no change and no warning.
confirmedRules.given: An active todo 'Pay rent' that is already done=true (or an open todo with done=false)
confirmedRules.when: The client sends PUT /todo/{id} with {"done": true} (or {"done": false} for the open todo)
confirmedRules.then: The server returns HTTP 200 with done unchanged (true, or false). The mark-done branch reads the stored title and description and writes them back as they are. No 'already done' or 'already open' message or conflict code is returned.
confirmedRules.parameters: Mark-done trigger: payload.done is truthy (todo_service.py:55). Reopen trigger: done supplied and falsy, written as-is by the generic partial update (repository.py:77-78). No status precondition exists on either path.
edgeCases: The pinned pydantic 2.11 parses 'done' loosely because update_todo_schema.py:10 sets no strict mode. {"done": "yes"}, {"done": 1}, {"done": "on"} or {"done": "true"} all mark the todo done. {"done": "no"}, {"done": 0} or {"done": "off"} reopen it.

Mark-done reads the todo and writes it in two separate database sessions (todo_service.py:91-95 calls repository.get_to_do_entry and then repository.update_to_do). If the todo is soft-deleted between the two steps, the write finds nothing and the caller gets 404.
The mark-done branch writes back the stored title and description without re-running sanitisation (todo_service.py:94). Mark-done therefore cannot fail on input validation.
The tests exercise Open->Done only, against a mocked repository (backend/tests/test_service/integration/test_mark_todo_done_integration.py:30-58). Done->Done and Open->Open are untested.

confirmedRules.name: Failed create, edit and delete requests are resent once automatically; a resend after a lost response reports a false failure
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The web client resends every failed create, edit or delete exactly once. Create and delete are not repeatable on the server (a repeated create gives 409, a repeated delete gives 404), so if the first attempt succeeded but its response was lost, the user is told the action failed.
confirmedRules.given: A user creates 'Buy milk' with client-generated id A. The first POST /todo commits on the server, but the response is lost (timeout or connection reset).
confirmedRules.when: React Query automatically resends the same POST /todo with id A (mutations retry: 1)
confirmedRules.then: The server answers 409 'ToDo already exists'. The UI removes the optimistic row and shows the toast 'Failed to create todo — API Error 409: ToDo already exists' with a Retry button. The follow-up list refetch then shows 'Buy milk', because it was in fact created. Delete behaves the same way: the resent DELETE returns 404 'ToDo not found', a 'Failed to delete todo' toast appears, and the row reappears until the refetch removes it.
confirmedRules.parameters: Mutation retry count = 1 (queryClient.ts:11-13). Query retry count = 1 (queryClient.ts:8). React Query v5 (^5.90.10) retries regardless of HTTP status.
edgeCases: Retries also fire for permanent 4xx rejections. A title containing a blocklisted word (for example 'or') is sent twice and rejected twice with 400 before the error toast appears.
An update resent after a lost response is harmless, because the same field values are written again.
The 'Todo deleted' success toast has already been shown before any of this happens (TodoDeleteButton.tsx:16-20). The user can therefore see a success toast and a failure toast for the same delete.
The initial list load is also retried once before the error state appears (queryClient.ts:8).
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should creating with an id that already exists and is identical, or deleting a todo that is already deleted, be treated as success, so that automatic or manual resends are safe? Or should the client stop resending non-repeatable operations?

confirmedRules.name: The toast 'Retry' resends the original request unchanged and skips the normal success handling
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a create, edit or delete fails, the error toast offers a Retry button. Retry resends exactly what was first submitted, including the same todo id and text, but on success it neither clears the form, closes the editor, nor shows a success message.
confirmedRules.given: A user typed 'Buy milk', the create failed with 500, and the error toast shows Retry
confirmedRules.when: The user edits the input to 'Buy oat milk' and then clicks Retry
confirmedRules.then: POST /todo is resent with the original id and title 'Buy milk', not 'Buy oat milk'. If it succeeds, no 'Todo created' toast appears and the input still shows 'Buy oat milk'. After an edit Retry succeeds, the edit form stays open and no 'Todo updated' toast appears.
confirmedRules.parameters: Toast default duration 5000 ms; Retry action label 'Retry' (useToast.ts:12-21). The Retry handlers call mutate(todoData) or mutate(updateData) without the onSuccess/onError callbacks that the original submit attaches.
edgeCases: A failed Retry raises no new error toast or Retry offer, because no per-call onError is attached. Only the hook-level rollback and refetch run (useCreateTodo.ts:41-50).
Retrying a delete resends DELETE for the same id. If the first attempt actually succeeded, the resend gets 404.
The id is fixed when the user first submits (TodoForm.tsx:48-52), so every Retry reuses it.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: After a successful Retry the UI does not reset the create input, close the edit form, or confirm success. The user cannot tell that the retry worked, and may submit the todo again (creating a duplicate with a new id).

confirmedRules.name: Create-form submission lifecycle: input locked while saving, cleared on success, kept on failure
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: After a valid title is submitted, the add-todo input is disabled until the server answers. On success the input is emptied and 'Todo created' is shown. On failure the typed text stays in the box and an error toast with Retry is shown.
confirmedRules.given: An empty add-todo input
confirmedRules.when: The user types 'Buy groceries' and presses Enter, and the server accepts it
confirmedRules.then: The input is disabled while the request is pending, then cleared, and a success toast 'Todo created / Your todo has been added successfully' appears. If the server rejects the request, the input keeps 'Buy groceries', becomes editable again, and the toast 'Failed to create todo' with Retry appears.
confirmedRules.parameters: Success toast title 'Todo created'; failure toast title 'Failed to create todo'. Input disabled while createTodo.isPending is true (TodoForm.tsx:87).
edgeCases: Submission is Enter-only: there is no Add button.
An inline validation error is cleared as soon as the user types again (TodoForm.tsx:33-36).

confirmedRules.name: Inline edit lifecycle: Viewing -> Editing -> Viewing on save or cancel; stays in Editing on failure
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Clicking Edit opens an editor pre-filled with the current title and hides the Edit and Delete buttons. Save leaves edit mode only when the server confirms the change. Cancel discards the changes without contacting the server.
confirmedRules.given: A todo 'Original todo' in viewing mode
confirmedRules.when: The user clicks Edit, changes the text to 'Changed text', and clicks Cancel
confirmedRules.then: No request is sent, the editor closes, and the item still shows 'Original todo'. If the user clicks Save instead and the server returns 200, the editor closes and 'Todo updated' is shown. If the server fails, the editor stays open with the edited text and the toast 'Failed to update todo' with Retry is shown.
confirmedRules.parameters: Editor seeded with initialTitle (TodoEditForm.tsx:15). Save is disabled while a validation error is shown (TodoEditForm.tsx:101) and re-enabled on the next keystroke (TodoEditForm.tsx:39-41).
edgeCases: A todo cannot be deleted while it is being edited, because the Delete button is hidden (TodoItem.tsx:19-26).
The editor has no Enter-to-save: only the Save button submits, since the input is not inside a form.
The UI does not know a todo's done status, so done todos are edited the same way. They stay done because the edit payload omits 'done'.
The editor is seeded once when it opens. If the title changes elsewhere while the editor is open, Save overwrites that change.

confirmedRules.name: No one can add todos while the list is loading or has failed to load
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The main screen is in one of four states: loading, error, empty or populated. The add-todo input exists only in the empty and populated states, so users cannot create todos while the list is loading or has failed to load.
confirmedRules.given: The backend returns 500 for GET /todo
confirmedRules.when: The page loads (after one automatic retry)
confirmedRules.then: The screen shows only an error box reading 'API Error 500: Internal error' and a Retry button. The add-todo input is not rendered. If the list loads with zero items, the input is shown with the message 'No todos yet. Add one above!'.
confirmedRules.parameters: Empty-state text 'No todos yet. Add one above!' (TodoList.tsx:31-35). The error fallback text 'Failed to load todos' is used only when the error is not an Error instance (TodoList.tsx:17). List query retry = 1.
edgeCases: While loading, only a spinner is shown (TodoList.tsx:11), so the form is unavailable there too.
The Retry button re-runs the list query only (TodoList.tsx:18).

confirmedRules.name: The list on screen refreshes only after the user's own changes; it is treated as fresh for 5 minutes
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The web client does not poll the server or refresh when the window regains focus. Changes made in another tab, by another user, or directly through the API stay invisible until this user creates, edits or deletes something, or reloads the page.
confirmedRules.given: Two browser tabs show the same list containing 'Pay rent'
confirmedRules.when: Tab B deletes 'Pay rent' and the user then edits 'Pay rent' in tab A without reloading
confirmedRules.then: Tab A still shows 'Pay rent'. The edit fails with 'API Error 404: ToDo not found', the optimistic change is rolled back, and the follow-up refetch finally removes the row.
confirmedRules.parameters: staleTime = 300,000 ms (5 min); gcTime = 600,000 ms (10 min); refetchOnWindowFocus = false; no refetchInterval (queryClient.ts:5-9). Every mutation invalidates the ['todos'] query when it settles.
edgeCases: Remounting the list within 5 minutes reuses cached data without asking the server again.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is a list that can be up to several minutes out of date acceptable, or must the rewrite show other users' and tabs' changes (by polling, refresh on focus, or push updates)?

confirmedRules.name: The last-updated timestamp is filled in by the database at creation, even though the application sets it to empty
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A new todo's 'updated_at' is intended to be empty, but the database fills it with its own current time when the row is inserted. It is never changed afterwards, and on a non-UTC server it can read as earlier than 'created_at'.
confirmedRules.given: A SQLite-backed server whose local time is 2026-10-03 14:00:00 CEST (UTC+2)
confirmedRules.when: A todo is created: the builder sets created_at = 2026-10-03 14:00:00 (local, no timezone) and updated_at = None, and the row is inserted
confirmedRules.then: The ORM leaves the None-valued updated_at out of the INSERT, so the mapped column default func.now() (rendered as SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, which is UTC) stores updated_at = 2026-10-03 12:00:00. A later GET /todo/{id} returns updated_at two hours earlier than created_at. No later edit changes it.
confirmedRules.parameters: Mapped-table default: updated_at default=func.now() (database.py:96). created_at comes from Python datetime.now() in server local time (todo_entry_builder.py:30). Pinned SQLAlchemy 2.0.43; its INSERT logic skips None values for columns that have defaults (library behaviour, verified in sqlalchemy/orm/persistence.py _collect_insert_commands).
edgeCases: This is the creation-time case of the already-catalogued 'updated_at never maintained' rule. The value is not null after creation, it is the insert time.
The response to the create call is built from the in-memory object (todo_service.py:43), so it may differ from what a later GET returns.
On PostgreSQL or MySQL (allowed by DATABASE_URL), now() returns the database server's time with its own timezone rules, so the offset differs.
Unit tests only check that updated_at is None on the object handed to a mocked repository (backend/tests/test_service/unit/test_create_todo.py:236), so this behaviour is untested.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should a newly created todo have updated_at empty, equal to created_at, or the insert time? And should all timestamps be stored in UTC?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The app and the database disagree on the initial value, and they use different clocks (server local time versus database UTC). This yields updated_at earlier than created_at.

confirmedRules.name: The domain model's own default for the 'deleted' flag is not false
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every new todo is meant to start as not deleted, but the todo data class's default for 'deleted' is a SQLAlchemy column-configuration object rather than false. Only the builder's explicit 'deleted=False' keeps new todos correct.
confirmedRules.given: Code that creates a ToDoEntryData(id, title, description, created_at, updated_at) without passing 'deleted'
confirmedRules.when: The object is built and saved
confirmedRules.then: 'deleted' holds the mapped_column(...) object (truthy, not a boolean), while 'done' correctly defaults to False. The only production path, ToDoEntryBuilder, always passes deleted=False, so today's behaviour is correct.
confirmedRules.parameters: models/todo.py:17 sets `deleted: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(default=False, name='deleted')` on a plain @dataclass. The table-level default is deleted=False (database.py:97).
edgeCases: The test factories also pass deleted=False explicitly (backend/tests/test_data/factories.py:15-27), so the faulty default is never exercised.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Engineering to confirm: can ToDoEntryData ever be created without an explicit 'deleted' value (imports, scripts, a future restore feature)? The rewrite should make 'not deleted' the explicit default.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: In a plain dataclass, the default for 'deleted' is the SQLAlchemy column-configuration object, not the boolean False.

confirmedRules.name: API responses always report deleted = false
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every todo the API returns includes a 'deleted' flag, but deleted todos are never returned, so the flag always reads false and tells the client nothing.
confirmedRules.given: An active todo
confirmedRules.when: It is returned by create, get, update or list
confirmedRules.then: The payload contains "deleted": false. A soft-deleted todo is never returned at all (get and update give 404, list leaves it out), so "deleted": true never appears.
confirmedRules.parameters: ToDoSchema.deleted default False; the read queries filter deleted.is_(False).
edgeCases: The front-end type declares the field, and optimistic inserts hard-code deleted:false, but no UI reads it.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the rewrite drop 'deleted' from the public contract, or keep it for a planned restore or trash view (README 'Further steps')?

confirmedRules.name: Users see failures as 'API Error <status>: <detail>' with no reason why input was rejected
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When the server rejects a request, the user sees a toast built from the HTTP status and the server's one-line detail. A validation rejection reads only 'Bad request', so users are never told which word or character was refused.
confirmedRules.given: A user enters the title 'Call mom or dad', which contains the blocklisted whole word 'or'
confirmedRules.when: They submit the todo
confirmedRules.then: The backend returns 400 with detail 'Bad request', and the toast shows 'Failed to create todo' / 'API Error 400: Bad request' with a Retry button that will fail the same way.
confirmedRules.parameters: Message format `API Error ${status}: ${detail || statusText}` (client.ts:18). Server details: 'ToDo already exists' (409), 'ToDo not found' (404), 'Bad request' (400), 'Internal error' (500).
edgeCases: FastAPI schema-validation errors (422) return 'detail' as a list of objects, so the toast reads 'API Error 422: [object Object]' (client.ts:63-64).
If the error body is not JSON, the HTTP status text is shown instead (client.ts:60-67).
When a delete fails, the error toast appears after a 'Todo deleted' success toast has already been shown.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should users be told why their input was rejected (for example, which word is not allowed)? Or should the blocklist be dropped so that ordinary words like 'or' and 'update' are accepted?

confirmedRules.name: Title length is counted in different units by the UI (UTF-16 code units) and the database (Unicode characters)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Both sides enforce a '255 character' title limit, but the screen counts each emoji or other non-BMP character as 2 while the database counts it as 1. So the UI limit is stricter than the server's, and a todo with a server-valid title can become impossible to edit in the UI.
confirmedRules.given: A todo whose title is 200 copies of the emoji U+1F389, created directly through POST /todo. The database CHECK length(title) <= 255 sees 200 characters and accepts it.
confirmedRules.when: The user clicks Edit in the web UI and then clicks Save without changing anything
confirmedRules.then: The edit form computes title.length = 400 and shows '-145 characters remaining' (255 - 400; the hint shows whenever remaining < 50). Save is refused with 'Todo title cannot exceed 255 characters' and the Save button disables until the user types. In the create box, maxLength=255 stops input at 127 such emoji (254 code units), even though the server would accept up to 255.
confirmedRules.parameters: MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 255, counted in UTF-16 code units (JS String.length and the HTML maxLength attribute), hardcoded separately in TodoForm.tsx:7 and TodoEditForm.tsx:6. Database CHECK: length(title) <= 255 and length(description) <= 255, counted in Unicode code points (SQLite length()). Near-limit hint threshold: remaining < 50.
edgeCases: Verified: 200 x U+1F389 gives Python len = 200, SQLite length() = 200, JS .length = 400
255 emoji insert successfully into the CHECK-constrained table; 256 plain ASCII characters are rejected

The remaining-characters counter uses the untrimmed length (item.length) while validation uses the trimmed length, so leading or trailing spaces lower the counter but are not counted against the limit
Combining sequences (for example 'e' + U+0301) count per code point in both systems, so there is no discrepancy for them
An HTML input whose initial value is longer than maxLength is not truncated: the user can delete characters but not add any
The UI never shows a description length counter because it always sends a fixed placeholder
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The UI and the server use different definitions of 'character'. Users who rely on emoji or other non-BMP characters (an explicitly tested use case, see backend/tests/test_data/constants.py:54-60) get a lower limit in the UI, and titles valid on the server cannot be re-saved from the edit form. The rewrite should pick one counting unit (code points or grapheme clusters) and use it in every layer.

confirmedRules.name: An embedded NUL character bypasses the 255-character limit on SQLite
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The only server-side length check is the database CHECK on length(title)/length(description). SQLite's length() stops counting at the first NUL character, so a title such as 'a' + NUL + 1,000 more letters is stored in full.
confirmedRules.given: POST /todo with a valid UUID and title "a\u0000" followed by 1,000 'b' characters (1,002 characters in total)
confirmedRules.when: The todo is saved to the SQLite database
confirmedRules.then: Pydantic accepts the string, strip() does not remove NUL, and the SQL blocklist regex does not match it. The CHECK sees length() = 1 and passes, so a 1,002-character title is stored and the request returns 200. By contrast, a 256-character plain title fails the CHECK and comes back as 409 'ToDo already exists'.
confirmedRules.parameters: CHECK length(title) <= 255 (title_length_check), CHECK length(description) <= 255 (description_length_check). There is no application-layer length check.
edgeCases: Verified in an in-memory SQLite database with the same CHECK: inserting 'a\x00' + 'b'*1000 succeeded and read back with length 1002
Applies equally to description and to the update path, which writes through the same table
The web UI cannot type a NUL, so this is reachable only through direct API calls
database.py:33 also allows postgresql:// URLs. PostgreSQL rejects NUL characters in text values, so these rows could not be migrated as-is
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The 255-character business limit depends on a database quirk rather than an explicit validation. Oversized and NUL-containing rows can already exist in production data and would break a migration to PostgreSQL. The rewrite should validate length (and reject control characters) in the application layer, and the migration needs to scan for such rows.

confirmedRules.name: 'Blank title' is judged by different whitespace rules in the UI and the server, and invisible titles are accepted
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The UI decides a title is empty using JavaScript trim(), and the server uses Python strip(). They remove different sets of invisible characters, and neither removes zero-width spaces, so some titles are rejected on one side only and visually blank titles get through both.
confirmedRules.given: Three candidate titles: (a) two zero-width spaces U+200B, (b) a single zero-width no-break space U+FEFF, (c) a pasted unit-separator control character U+001F
confirmedRules.when: Each is submitted, through the UI or directly to the API
confirmedRules.then: (a) Both UI and server accept it, so a todo with a visually empty title is created. (b) The UI rejects it with 'Todo title cannot be empty', but POST /todo accepts and stores it. (c) The UI accepts it and sends it. The server strips it to empty and rejects it: 422 on create (Pydantic schema validator) or 400 'Bad request' on update (service validate_required).
confirmedRules.parameters: UI whitespace set: ECMAScript trim() (Zs category, TAB/VT/FF, U+FEFF, LF/CR/U+2028/U+2029). Server whitespace set: Python str.strip() (Zs, TAB/LF/VT/FF/CR, U+001C-U+001F, U+0085, U+2028/U+2029; not U+FEFF). Neither set includes U+200B.
edgeCases: Verified empirically: U+FEFF is trimmed by JS but not by Python; U+001C, U+001F and U+0085 are trimmed by Python but not by JS; U+200B is trimmed by neither
U+00A0 (no-break space) and U+3000 (ideographic space) are trimmed by both, so those cases match
The same blank-after-trim title gets 422 on create but 400 on update, because different layers reject it
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: There is no single definition of a 'blank' title. Visually empty todos can be created, and the UI and server disagree on some inputs. The rewrite should define the trimmed character set once (ideally including zero-width and format characters) and share it between client and server.

confirmedRules.name: Schema-level rejections (HTTP 422) are shown to the user as 'API Error 422: [object Object]'
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: For 400/404/409/500 errors the server sends a text 'detail', but for request-schema failures (422) FastAPI sends a list of error objects. The UI pastes that list straight into the message, so users see '[object Object]'.
confirmedRules.given: The UI submits a new todo whose title the browser considers non-blank but Python strips to empty, for example a pasted U+001F
confirmedRules.when: POST /todo fails ToDoCreateScheme's title validator and returns 422 with detail = [{type, loc, msg, input}]
confirmedRules.then: handleResponse takes errorBody.detail (an array, which is truthy) as the message text. ApiClientError builds 'API Error 422: [object Object]' (or '[object Object],[object Object]' when there are several errors), and that string appears as the error toast description.
confirmedRules.parameters: Message template: 'API Error {status}: {detail || statusText}'. ApiError.detail is typed as string but receives an array for 422 responses.
edgeCases: Verified: String([{msg:'x'}]) yields '[object Object]' in Node

Blank or whitespace-only title: 422 on create (backend/tests/test_api/test_api_endpoints.py:107-129 asserts 422) but 400 on update (backend/tests/test_api/test_update_to_do.py:132-143 accepts either 400 or 422, so the asymmetry is untested)
A missing id, malformed UUID, or non-integer limit/page also produces 422 with an array detail
A non-JSON 500 (for example an unhandled list error) falls back to statusText, giving 'API Error 500: Internal Server Error'
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The UI's error contract assumes detail is always a string. The rewrite should normalise validation errors to one shape and one status code for the same rule, whichever layer enforces it.

confirmedRules.name: Result toasts, including the Retry offer, disappear after 5 seconds of active page time and cannot be dismissed manually
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every success or failure notice disappears on its own after 5 seconds (the timer pauses while the page is idle or hidden), so the one-click Retry after a failed create, edit or delete is only offered for that window.
confirmedRules.given: A create request that fails with a server error, while the user keeps the tab in the foreground
confirmedRules.when: The error toast 'Failed to create todo' appears with a Retry action
confirmedRules.then: The toast and its Retry button stay visible for 5,000 ms and then auto-dismiss. After that the user can only retry by submitting the form again (the typed text is kept). There is no close button, because 'closable' is never set.
confirmedRules.parameters: duration = 5000 ms (default in useAppToast, never overridden by callers); placement = bottom-end; pauseOnPageIdle = true; Retry action label = 'Retry'.
edgeCases: If the tab is hidden or the page is idle, the 5-second countdown pauses (pauseOnPageIdle)
Success toasts use the same 5-second duration
None of the callers in the components passes a custom duration
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the Retry offer after a failed save stay until the user dismisses it, or is a 5-second auto-dismiss (paused while the tab is hidden or idle) the intended behavior? Also, confirm whether the Chakra/Zag pauseOnPageIdle semantics (pause while the document is hidden) are what the business expects.

confirmedRules.name: No request-rate limit or quota on creating todos, even though a rate-limiting library is declared
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Any caller can create, edit or delete todos as often as they like, and there is no cap on how many todos exist. A rate-limiting dependency (slowapi) is listed but never wired in.
confirmedRules.given: A client that sends 10,000 POST /todo requests with distinct UUIDs in one minute
confirmedRules.when: The requests reach the API
confirmedRules.then: All of them are accepted. No limiter middleware or decorator is registered, and the repository inserts without counting existing rows.
