confirmedRules.parameters: Declared dependency slowapi >= 0.1.9 (pyproject.toml:19). No imports of slowapi, Limiter, or any rate-limit configuration anywhere in backend or frontend code (grep returned no matches).
edgeCases: The e2e harness cleans up by listing up to limit=1000 rows (frontend/e2e/global-setup.ts:8), which implicitly assumes no server-side cap on page size
Combined with the missing ownership checks recorded earlier, a single client can fill the shared list without bound
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Was a per-client rate limit or a maximum number of todos intended (slowapi is a declared dependency)? If so, what limits apply (requests per minute per IP or user, maximum active todos), and should the rewrite enforce them?

confirmedRules.name: Same blank-title rule is rejected with 422 on create but 400 on edit (two-layer validation)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Input is checked in two places: checks built into the request schema (create title blank or missing, bad id format, wrong field types) fail with HTTP 422 and a list of reasons per field, while checks in the service layer (blocked words and symbols, blank title on edit) fail with HTTP 400 and only the text 'Bad request'. So the one business rule 'title must not be blank' gives a different outcome depending on whether you are creating or editing.
confirmedRules.given: An existing open todo X titled 'Buy milk'
confirmedRules.when: (a) POST /todo with {id: <new uuid>, title: "   "}; (b) PUT /todo/X with {title: "   "}
confirmedRules.then: (a) HTTP 422 with detail [{loc:["body","title"], msg:"Value error, title must not be null."}] and nothing stored; (b) HTTP 400 with {"detail":"Bad request"}, and X keeps the title 'Buy milk'
confirmedRules.parameters: Schema-layer reject status = 422 (FastAPI/pydantic default, list-shaped detail); service-layer reject status = 400, fixed detail 'Bad request' (api.py:48, api.py:70); schema message 'title must not be null.' (create_todo_schema.py:28)
edgeCases: POST with title 'Tea or coffee' passes the schema and fails the service blocklist, so it returns 400, not 422
POST without an id, or with id 'not-a-valid-uuid', returns 422 (test_api_endpoints.py:131-141)
PUT body {"title": 5} returns 422 (wrong type), while PUT {"title": ""} returns 400

The web client builds its message as 'API Error {status}: {detail}' and expects detail to be a string (client.ts:63-64, 18). A 422 detail is a list, so the user would see 'API Error 422: [object Object]'
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: One rule, two status codes. The API test for blank-title edits accepts either 400 or 422 (test_update_to_do.py:143), so the contract was never pinned down. The 422 detail list also renders as '[object Object]' in the UI. Note: the client.ts citation is legacy/basictodo/frontend/src/services/api/client.ts:58-69.

confirmedRules.name: Invalid edits are silently accepted when the same request marks the todo done
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If an edit request contains done=true, the system skips every title and description check for that request, so a blank or blocked title that would normally be rejected returns success instead. The edit is quietly dropped and the caller gets no error.
confirmedRules.given: An open todo X titled 'Buy milk' with description 'Oat milk'
confirmedRules.when: PUT /todo/X with {done: true, title: "   ", description: "DROP everything; --"}
confirmedRules.then: HTTP 200; X is now done=true and still titled 'Buy milk' with description 'Oat milk'; no 400 is raised. The same body without done (or with done=false) returns 400 'Bad request'
confirmedRules.parameters: Branch condition: payload.done is truthy (todo_service.py:55). Title and description validation happens only after that branch (todo_service.py:59-62)
edgeCases: {done: true, title: null} returns 200 (done), even though {title: null} alone causes a server error
{done: true} on a soft-deleted or unknown id returns 404 (todo_service.py:91-93)
{done: true, title: 'New title'} with a valid title also drops the title change without telling the caller
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Invalid input gets a success response, and the client cannot tell its other changes were thrown away. A rewrite should either validate every field supplied or reject mixed requests.

confirmedRules.name: An edit with no recognised fields succeeds as a no-op
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An edit request with an empty body, or with only fields the system doesn't know, is not rejected. It returns success and leaves the todo exactly as it was.
confirmedRules.given: An open todo X titled 'Buy milk'
confirmedRules.when: PUT /todo/X with {} or {"deleted": false} or {"priority": "high"}
confirmedRules.then: HTTP 200 with X returned unchanged. Unknown keys are dropped silently (pydantic default extra='ignore'), and nothing tells the caller that nothing changed
confirmedRules.parameters: Updatable keys: title, description, done (update_todo_schema.py:8-10). Unknown-key policy: ignore (framework default, no explicit model config)
edgeCases: PUT {} on a soft-deleted or unknown id returns 404, because the repository lookup filters out deleted rows (repository.py:72-76)
{"deleted": false} cannot restore a soft-deleted todo: it returns 404
{"done": false} alone is not a no-op: it reopens the todo

confirmedRules.name: The done flag accepts loosely typed values such as 'yes', 'on', '1' and 1
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The 'done' field on edit isn't limited to JSON true/false: text such as 'yes', 'on', 'true', '1' or the number 1 marks the todo done, and 'no', 'off', 'false', '0' or 0 reopens it. Anything else is rejected with 422.
confirmedRules.given: An open todo X
confirmedRules.when: PUT /todo/X with {"done": "yes"}
confirmedRules.then: HTTP 200 and X is marked done (same as {"done": true}). Then PUT /todo/X with {"done": "off"} returns 200 and X is open again. PUT with {"done": "maybe"} or {"done": 2} returns 422
confirmedRules.parameters: done: Optional[bool] with no strict mode. pydantic 2.11.5 lax coercion accepts true/false, 0/1, and the case-insensitive strings 'true','false','yes','no','on','off','y','n','t','f','1','0'
edgeCases: {"done": "false"} counts as false, so it does not take the mark-done branch. It runs the normal update and sets done=false
{"done": null} skips mark-done, then tries to store NULL in a NOT NULL column (already catalogued as a server error)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the API accept only JSON true/false for 'done', or does any client depend on string or number forms ('yes', '1', 1)? A rewrite in another stack will not reproduce pydantic's lax coercion unless this is decided.

confirmedRules.name: Web UI does not pre-check the server's blocked words and symbols
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The screen only checks that a title isn't blank and is at most 255 characters, so ordinary titles the server always rejects (any containing 'or', 'update', 'create', 'select', ';' or '--') get through the screen and fail only after they are sent.
confirmedRules.given: The user is on the main screen with the create form
confirmedRules.when: They type 'Tea or coffee' (or 'Update CV', 'Call mom; then dentist') and press Enter
confirmedRules.then: Screen validation passes, the todo briefly appears (optimistic add), the server returns 400 'Bad request', the entry is rolled back, and a toast says 'Failed to create todo' with 'API Error 400: Bad request' and a Retry button that will fail the same way every time
confirmedRules.parameters: Client checks: trimmed title non-empty; trimmed length <= MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 255. Server blocklist: --, ;, /*, */, xp_cmdshell, drop, delete, insert, update, exec, execute, union, select, shutdown, create, alter, rename, truncate, declare, OR (whole words, case-insensitive)
edgeCases: Editing an existing todo to 'Select venue' fails the same way: the edit form stays open with the 'Failed to update todo' toast
A title made only of U+0085 (next-line control character) survives JavaScript trim() but Python strip() removes it, so the server returns 422 and the toast reads 'API Error 422: [object Object]'
A title made only of U+FEFF is blocked by the UI as empty, although the server would accept it
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Client and server validation rules have drifted apart. Users get a generic error and a Retry for a rejection that can never succeed.

confirmedRules.name: No request rate limiting on any endpoint, although a rate-limit library is declared
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Any caller can create, edit, delete or list todos as often as they like. A rate-limiting library (slowapi) is listed as a dependency, but it is never imported or applied, so no throttling policy is in effect.
confirmedRules.given: A single client with no credentials
confirmedRules.when: It sends 10,000 POST /todo requests in one minute
confirmedRules.then: Every valid request is processed and stored. No 429 response is ever returned, because only CORS middleware is registered on the app
confirmedRules.parameters: slowapi>=0.1.9 declared (pyproject.toml:19); registered middleware: CORSMiddleware only, allow_origins=['http://localhost:5173'] (api.py:23-29)
edgeCases: CORS limits only browsers on other origins; scripts and non-browser clients are not restricted
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Was per-client rate limiting meant to be part of the product (slowapi is a declared dependency but unused)? If so, what limits per endpoint, and what should the user see when throttled?

confirmedRules.name: Failed delete shows no error and the item quietly comes back after a 'Todo deleted' message
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When the server rejects a delete, the user gets no failure message and no Retry button. They have already seen 'Todo deleted', and the todo simply reappears in the list.
confirmedRules.given: Todo 'Pay rent' is shown in the web list. The delete endpoint will fail, for example with HTTP 500 or a network error.
confirmedRules.when: The user clicks 'Delete Todo' and confirms the dialog
confirmedRules.then: A 'Todo deleted' success toast appears straight away (TodoDeleteButton.tsx:15-20). onMutate removes 'Pay rent' from the cached list before the request is sent (useDeleteTodo.ts:18-26), so the TodoItem and its TodoDeleteButton unmount. The request fails, is retried once (queryClient.ts:12) and fails again. The hook-level onError puts 'Pay rent' back in the list (useDeleteTodo.ts:31-36). The 'Failed to delete todo' toast with Retry (TodoDeleteButton.tsx:23-30) is attached to the unmounted component's mutate() call, and TanStack Query v5 does not run per-call callbacks after the component unmounts, so it never shows. The user sees a success message followed by the todo silently coming back.
confirmedRules.and: If the failure was a 404 because the todo was already deleted elsewhere, the item comes back briefly and then disappears again when onSettled refetches the list. Either way, no failure message is shown.
confirmedRules.parameters: Mutation retry = 1 (queryClient.ts:12); @tanstack/react-query ^5.90.10 (package.json:21); confirm text 'Do you really want to delete this item?'
edgeCases: Server 500 or network failure: item reappears permanently with no explanation after a success toast
Server 404 (already deleted in another tab): item flickers back, then the refetch removes it again
The Retry action for delete can never be reached through the normal flow
onMutate skips removal only when no list is cached ('if (!old) return old'). In that case the button stays mounted and the error toast would show.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should a failed delete always tell the user and offer a retry? And should 'Todo deleted' appear only after the server confirms? (Engineering should confirm with a forced-500 test that the onError toast never fires in the current build.)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Two problems combine: the success toast is shown optimistically, and the error toast lives in a component that the optimistic removal unmounts. Together they hide every delete failure from the user.

confirmedRules.name: Cancelling an edit while the save is in flight hides the outcome and can silently revert the title
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: While a save is in progress, the edit box stays editable and Cancel stays clickable. Cancelling at that point closes the form, so the user never learns whether the save worked. If it failed, the new title quietly turns back into the old one.
confirmedRules.given: Todo titled 'Buy milk' is open in the inline edit form, and the user changes the text to 'Buy oat milk'
confirmedRules.when: The user clicks Save and then clicks Cancel before the server responds
confirmedRules.then: The list shows 'Buy oat milk' straight away (optimistic update, useUpdateTodo.ts:19-34). Cancel sets isEditing=false (TodoItem.tsx:33), which unmounts TodoEditForm. If the save succeeds, no 'Todo updated' toast appears. If it fails (after 1 automatic retry), useUpdateTodo.ts:39-44 restores 'Buy milk', and the 'Failed to update todo' toast with Retry (TodoEditForm.tsx:62-68) never shows because its component is gone.
confirmedRules.and: The create form locks its input while saving (TodoForm.tsx:87: disabled={createTodo.isPending}). The edit form does not: the input at TodoEditForm.tsx:78-84 has no disabled flag, and Cancel (line 105) is never disabled. Text typed during the save is not sent, and it is thrown away when the success path closes the form.
confirmedRules.parameters: Save button shows a loading state only (TodoEditForm.tsx:100); Cancel has no disabled condition; mutation retry = 1
edgeCases: Save succeeds after Cancel: change is stored but never confirmed to the user
Save fails after Cancel: title reverts in the list with no message
User keeps typing during the save: the extra text is not saved and is dropped when the form closes on success
User reopens Edit before the response: the new form starts from the optimistic title, and the old save's outcome is still not reported
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: While a save is pending, should the edit form be locked (input and Cancel disabled), as the create form is? And must the outcome of a save always be reported, even if the user has closed the editor?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The create and edit forms handle an in-flight save differently, and the save outcome can be lost when the user cancels.

confirmedRules.name: Concurrent edits: last write wins with no conflict detection
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When two people edit the same todo, the later save silently overwrites the earlier one. Nothing checks whether the todo changed since the editor loaded it.
confirmedRules.given: Todo X titled 'Buy milk' is loaded in browser A and in browser B. The list cache counts as fresh for 5 minutes and is not refetched when the tab regains focus.
confirmedRules.when: A saves the title 'Buy oat milk' at 10:00. Then B, whose edit form still holds the 'Buy milk' it captured when opened (TodoEditForm.tsx:15), saves 'Buy whole milk' at 10:01.
confirmedRules.then: Both PUTs return 200. The stored title is 'Buy whole milk', and A's change is lost with no warning to either user. update_to_do loads the row by id plus deleted=false and applies the supplied fields (repository.py:72-78). TodoUpdateScheme has no version, ETag or expected-updated_at field, so no precondition can be expressed.
confirmedRules.and: Every UI save also sends description 'not implemented yet' (TodoEditForm.tsx:51), so a description edited concurrently through the API is overwritten too. Fields not sent in a PUT, such as done, are left as they are.
confirmedRules.parameters: No version or concurrency token exists; staleTime = 5 minutes (queryClient.ts:6); refetchOnWindowFocus = false (queryClient.ts:9)
edgeCases: A marks the todo done through the API while B renames it in the UI: done stays true, because B's PUT leaves done out
Two API clients PUT different titles at the same moment: whichever commits last is kept
updated_at is never maintained, so it cannot serve as a conflict check without changes
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is last-write-wins acceptable, or should the rewrite reject stale edits (for example with a version number or an If-Match check on updated_at) and tell the second editor?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Edits can be lost silently with no conflict detection. Because the UI treats the list as fresh for 5 minutes, stale edits are likely.

confirmedRules.name: Success and failure notifications, including the Retry offer, auto-dismiss after 5 seconds
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each notification after a create, edit or delete closes itself after 5 seconds, and that pause stops while the page is idle. A failure's Retry button can only be used during that window, and the user cannot close a notification early.
confirmedRules.given: Creating todo 'Call dentist' fails and the 'Failed to create todo' toast with a Retry action appears
confirmedRules.when: The user does not click Retry within 5 seconds while the page is active
confirmedRules.then: The toast and its Retry action disappear. The default duration is 5000 ms (useToast.ts:12), and the toaster pauses timers while the page is idle (pauseOnPageIdle: true, toaster.ts:5). Toasts appear at the bottom-right ('bottom-end', toaster.ts:4).
confirmedRules.and: useAppToast never sets 'closable', so no close button is rendered (toaster.tsx:32). Toasts go away only when they time out or the user clicks Retry.
confirmedRules.parameters: Toast duration = 5000 ms (default status 'info'); placement = bottom-end; pauseOnPageIdle = true; Retry label = 'Retry'; closable = not set
edgeCases: User switches tabs or leaves the page idle: the timer pauses and the Retry offer lasts longer
For a create failure, the typed text stays in the input, so the user can resubmit by pressing Enter after the toast expires
Several failures in a row stack separate toasts, each with its own 5-second window
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should failure notifications stay until the user dismisses them, so the Retry offer cannot expire unnoticed? Is 5 seconds the right lifetime for success messages?

confirmedRules.name: The 'done' status flag accepts loose truthy and falsy spellings
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The API does not require a true/false value for 'done'. Values such as "yes", "on", "1" or 1 mark a todo done, and "no", "off", "0" or 0 reopen it.
confirmedRules.given: Open todo X exists and is not deleted
confirmedRules.when: A client sends PUT /todo/X with body {"done": "yes"}, or "on", "1", "true", "Y", 1 or 1.0
confirmedRules.then: FastAPI parses the body into TodoUpdateScheme, where done is Optional[bool] (update_todo_schema.py:10). Pydantic's default lax mode turns the value into True, so the mark-done branch runs (todo_service.py:55-57) and the response is 200 with done=true.
confirmedRules.and: {"done": "no"}, "off", "0", "false", "n" or 0 becomes False. The non-done branch then stores done=false, which reopens a done todo (todo_service.py:59-68). {"done": "maybe"} or 2 is rejected with 422.
confirmedRules.parameters: Pydantic 2.11.5 (uv.lock:573-574), lax mode by default. Accepted true values: true, 1, 1.0, 'true', 't', 'yes', 'y', 'on', '1' (strings are case-insensitive). Accepted false values: false, 0, 0.0, 'false', 'f', 'no', 'n', 'off', '0'.
edgeCases: {"done": 0} reopens a completed todo just as {"done": false} does
{"done": "yes", "title": "New"}: the mark-done branch wins and the title is ignored
{"done": null} is a separate, already-known path that ends in a server error
The web UI never sends 'done', so only direct API clients reach this behavior
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the rewrite accept only JSON true/false for the completion flag (strict), or are clients known to send string or numeric forms that must keep working? (Not verified at runtime: pydantic is not installed in the analysis environment.)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: A completion flag that accepts free-form strings could let a typo or a mis-serialized client change a todo's status by accident (for example, "0" reopens it).

confirmedRules.name: Out-of-range page and page-size values are never rejected; the result depends on the arithmetic and the database engine
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The list endpoint accepts any whole number for page and page size. On the default SQLite store, page 0 or a negative page quietly returns the first page, a negative page size returns every active todo, and numbers too big for 64 bits cause a server error. Nothing is ever rejected as out of range.
confirmedRules.given: An SQLite-backed store holding 25 active (not deleted) todos. Skip is computed as (page - 1) x limit.
confirmedRules.when: A client calls GET /todo with page=0&limit=10, page=-3&limit=10, limit=-1, limit=-1&page=2, limit=-5&page=0, limit=0, and page=4611686018427387904 in turn.
confirmedRules.then: page=0 gives skip -10, which SQLite treats as 0, so the first 10 todos come back (same as page 1). page=-3 gives skip -40, again the first 10. limit=-1 gives all 25 (a negative LIMIT means no cap in SQLite). limit=-1&page=2 gives skip -1, still all 25. limit=-5&page=0 gives skip +5, so 20 todos starting at the 6th. limit=0 gives an empty list with results=0 and success=true. page=4611686018427387904 makes skip overflow 64 bits, which surfaces as an unmapped error and HTTP 500.
confirmedRules.parameters: skip = (page - 1) x limit. Defaults: limit=10, page=1. No minimum or maximum is enforced at the API, service or repository layer. SQLite rules: a negative OFFSET counts as 0 and a negative LIMIT means no cap. The largest bindable integer is 9,223,372,036,854,775,807. Allowed database schemes are sqlite://, postgresql:// and mysql:// (database.py:33).
edgeCases: A negative limit combined with page < 1 produces a positive skip. For example limit=-5&page=0 silently skips the first 5 rows.
list_todos (api.py:88-91) maps no exceptions, so any repository failure, including integer overflow, becomes a generic 500.

If DATABASE_URL points at PostgreSQL or MySQL (allowed by database.py:33), negative LIMIT/OFFSET values raise database errors, so the same request returns 500 instead of data. This comes from engine knowledge and was not run.
The API tests at test_list_to_do.py:191-289 mock the service and accept either 200 or 422 ('Should either cap or reject'), so the real arithmetic is never tested and the intended policy is undecided.
The e2e cleanup code (global-setup.ts:8, smoke.spec.ts:18, todo-validation.spec.ts:6) depends on limit=1000 meaning 'everything', i.e. on there being no page-size cap.
Because results equals the rows returned, limit=-1 is currently the only way to get a total count of active todos.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What ranges are allowed for page and page size (for example page >= 1 and 1 <= limit <= 100)? Should out-of-range values be rejected with 422 or clamped? Do any consumers rely on limit=-1 or a very large limit to fetch every todo?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: There is no bounds validation. Page <= 0 behaves like page 1, a negative limit removes the cap, a negative limit with page 0 skips rows, 64-bit overflow returns 500, and results change if the configured database engine changes. The SQLite outcomes were confirmed by running the same LIMIT/OFFSET arithmetic against an in-memory SQLite database. The SQLAlchemy layer itself was not run.

confirmedRules.name: Blocked SQL words only match at word boundaries: underscores and digits hide them, hyphens and accents don't
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The text filter rejects a blocked word, in any letter case, only when the characters on both sides are not letters, digits or underscores. Everyday words such as 'or', 'update', 'create' and 'exec' are refused even in hyphenated or accented phrases. The same words joined to an underscore or digit pass, and some real SQL syntax ('#', '||', WAITFOR) isn't blocked at all.
confirmedRules.given: A create or update request whose title is one of the strings below.
confirmedRules.when: The title goes through the input sanitizer.
confirmedRules.then: Rejected with 400 'Bad request': 'Call Anna or Ben' (or), 'Re-create slides' (create), 'Café-update' (update), 'décor or not' (or), 'Exec meeting' (exec), 'Pages 10--20' (--), 'path /*.txt' (/*), 'Buy milk; eggs' (;). Accepted: 'DROP_TABLE users', '1=1OR1=1', 'OR1=1', 'select2 venue', 'Execs meeting', 'Executed plan', 'updated CV', 'Doctor visit', 'Ordered parts', "It's a test", "admin'#", "1' || '1'='1", "WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'".
confirmedRules.parameters: Blocked anywhere in the text: '--', ';', '/*', '*/'. Blocked as whole words: xp_cmdshell, drop, delete, insert, update, exec, execute, union, select, shutdown, create, alter, rename, truncate, declare, or. Matching ignores letter case and uses Unicode-aware word boundaries (letters, digits and underscore count as word characters). The check runs on the raw text before trimming.
edgeCases: The integration test named 'time-based injection' (test_input_sanitizer_integration.py:89-93) passes only because its payload contains ';' and '--'. WAITFOR on its own is accepted.
MySQL '#' comments, '||' concatenation, and apostrophes or double quotes are all allowed.
A hyphen, apostrophe or accented letter next to a keyword still counts as a word boundary, so 'Re-create' and "x OR'1'='1" are rejected.
The rejection reason (which token matched) is only logged. The caller just gets 'Bad request'.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The filter blocks common to-do verbs and conjunctions (update, create, delete, select, execute, drop, or) yet lets real injection syntax through. Storage already uses ORM-bound parameters (repository.py:70-97), so the filter adds no real protection and mainly rejects legitimate titles. The exact regex was run in memory against every example above.

confirmedRules.name: The server accepts line breaks and tabs inside titles, but the web UI edits titles on a single line
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Server-side title validation trims only leading and trailing whitespace, so titles stored through the API can contain line breaks and tabs. The web UI shows and edits titles in a single-line box, so a multi-line title displays on one line, and any keystroke in the edit box removes its line breaks before saving.
confirmedRules.given: A todo created directly through the API with title "Line1\nLine2". The server returns 200 and stores the line break.
confirmedRules.when: A user opens the todo in the web UI, clicks Edit, types '!' at the end, and saves.
confirmedRules.then: The list shows the title as 'Line1 Line2' (whitespace collapses on screen). The edit box shows 'Line1Line2' because single-line HTML inputs drop CR/LF. After the keystroke the saved title is 'Line1Line2!', so the line break is lost and the description is overwritten with the placeholder. Clicking Save without typing sends the original "Line1\nLine2" unchanged, because the form state still holds the unsanitized initial value.
confirmedRules.parameters: Characters allowed in titles and descriptions: everything except the blocked tokens and words. Only leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed (Python str.strip).
edgeCases: Tabs inside text are kept ("Tab\there" is accepted unchanged, test_input_sanitizer.py:134-137).
A leading or trailing newline is removed by the trim. Interior ones stay.
Multi-line descriptions are explicitly expected (test_input_sanitizer_integration.py:49-53), but the UI never displays or edits descriptions.
Pasting multi-line text into the create box strips the line breaks in the browser, so only API clients can create multi-line titles.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Are titles meant to be single-line? Should the server reject or normalize CR/LF, tabs and other control characters in titles, and should descriptions keep multi-line text?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: A UI edit round trip silently changes multi-line titles, and the front end and back end disagree on which characters a title may contain. The UI part relies on standard HTML input sanitization and was not run in a browser.

confirmedRules.name: Create requests silently drop client-supplied status, deleted flag, timestamps and misspelled fields
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a todo is created, any field other than id, title and description is discarded without an error. A caller who sends done, deleted, created_at or a misspelled field name still gets a success response, and the todo is open, not deleted, and stamped with the server's current time.
confirmedRules.given: POST /todo with body {"id":"3f2b6c1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","title":"Pay rent","done":true,"deleted":true,"created_at":"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z","descripton":"before the 3rd"}
confirmedRules.when: The request is validated and the todo is built.
confirmedRules.then: The request succeeds with HTTP 200. The stored todo has done=false, deleted=false and created_at set to the server's current local time (not 2020-01-01). Its description is empty, because the misspelled 'descripton' key is silently ignored.
confirmedRules.parameters: Extra-field policy: ignore. This is the Pydantic v2 default, since ToDoCreateScheme sets no model_config (pydantic 2.11.5 per uv.lock:573-574). Fields the client may set: id, title, description.
edgeCases: A misspelled required field fails only indirectly. {"id":..., "titel":"x"} gets 422 because title is missing, not because 'titel' is unknown.
There is no way through the API to import historical todos with their original status or creation time.
Update requests behave the same way (unknown fields are ignored), as already catalogued for the update schema.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Typos in optional fields cause silent data loss with a success response. Clients that think they can create a todo already marked done get no warning.

confirmedRules.name: Input checks run before the existence and duplicate checks (400/422 beats 404/409)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If a request is invalid and also targets a ToDo that does not exist (or reuses an id that already exists), the system reports the bad input (400 or 422) instead of 'not found' (404) or 'already exists' (409). The one exception is a mark-done request, which checks existence first and skips input validation.
confirmedRules.given: No active ToDo with id 6f1c2a9e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 exists (either never created or soft-deleted), and a separate ToDo with id A already exists
confirmedRules.when: The client sends PUT /todo/6f1c2a9e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 with {"title": "Drop off parcel"}, or with {"title": "   "}
confirmedRules.then: The response is 400 'Bad request' and the database is never queried. The same PUT with {"title": "Buy milk"} returns 404 'ToDo not found'. With {"done": true, "title": "   "} it returns 404, because mark-done checks existence first and skips validation. On create, POST {"id": A, "title": "Select venue"} returns 400 (not 409), and POST {"id": A, "title": "  "} returns 422.
confirmedRules.parameters: Edit check order: (1) if done is truthy: existence check, then mark done; (2) title blank/blocklist check (400); (3) description blocklist check (400); (4) existence check inside repository update (404). Create check order: (1) schema checks: id is a UUID, title not blank (422); (2) builder blank/blocklist checks (400); (3) duplicate id or DB constraint at insert (409).
edgeCases: Soft-deleted ToDo plus an invalid title gives 400, not 404
Missing ToDo plus an invalid description only ({"description": "a; b"}) gives 400
Missing ToDo with done=false and an invalid title gives 400
Existing id plus an over-length title gives 409 either way, because both failures surface at insert as an integrity error
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should 'not found' / 'already exists' take priority over input-format errors in the new system, or is validating the payload first the intended contract for clients?

confirmedRules.name: List paging inputs are not range-checked: negative limit returns everything, page 0 or below returns page 1, and there is no maximum
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The list endpoint accepts any whole number for limit and page. On the default SQLite store, a negative limit means 'no limit', a page of zero or less quietly returns the first page, limit 0 returns an empty list, and there is no upper cap. The automated test cleanup depends on that missing cap (it calls limit=1000).
confirmedRules.given: 25 active ToDos in the default SQLite database
confirmedRules.when: The client calls GET /todo?limit=-1, GET /todo?page=0&limit=10, GET /todo?limit=0, and GET /todo?limit=10000
confirmedRules.then: limit=-1 returns 200 with all 25 items and results=25. page=0 computes offset (0-1)x10 = -10, which SQLite treats as 0, so it returns the same 10 items as page 1. limit=0 returns 200 with an empty list and results=0. limit=10000 returns all 25 (no cap). A non-integer such as limit=abc returns 422.
confirmedRules.parameters: Default limit=10 and page=1 (api.py:89). Offset = (page - 1) x limit (repository.py:93). No minimum or maximum bounds. SQLite reads LIMIT -1 as unlimited (SQLAlchemy's own SQLite dialect writes LIMIT -1 to mean 'no limit') and treats a negative OFFSET as 0. The e2e cleanup calls limit=1000.
edgeCases: limit=-1&page=3 gives offset -2, which becomes 0, so all rows are returned and page is ignored

PostgreSQL and MySQL URLs are allowed (database.py:33) and reject a negative LIMIT/OFFSET. The service wraps that as a repository error, and the list endpoint has no error mapping, so the client gets a bare 500
Every out-of-range test accepts either 200 or 422, so no intended policy is written down
With more than 1000 ToDos, the e2e cleanup leaves records behind
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What are the allowed ranges for limit and page (for example limit 1-100, page >= 1), and should out-of-range values be rejected with 422 or clamped? Does any consumer rely on limit=-1 or very large limits to fetch everything?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: A negative limit acts as 'return everything' and bypasses pagination. The outcome also depends on the database backend: SQLite returns all rows, while PostgreSQL fails with a 500.

confirmedRules.name: Create silently ignores fields the client is not allowed to set
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Extra fields in a create request, such as done, deleted, created_at or misspelled names, are thrown away without warning and the request still succeeds. A client therefore cannot create a ToDo that is already completed or backdated, and is never told its values were ignored.
confirmedRules.given: A client creates a ToDo with id 3b9d0c1e-1111-4222-8333-444455556666 and title 'Pay rent'
confirmedRules.when: POST /todo with {"id":"3b9d0c1e-1111-4222-8333-444455556666","title":"Pay rent","done":true,"created_at":"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z","descripton":"by Friday"}
confirmedRules.then: 200 success. The returned ToDo has done=false, deleted=false, created_at set to the server's current time, and description=null, because the misspelled 'descripton' was dropped. No 422 and no warning.
confirmedRules.parameters: Accepted create fields: id (UUID, required), title (required), description (optional). Extra-field policy: the framework default, which is to ignore them (no forbid setting on the model). The builder hard-codes done=False, deleted=False, created_at=now() and updated_at=None.
edgeCases: deleted=true on create is ignored
A wrong-case 'Title' leaves title missing, so the request fails with 422
Unknown business fields such as 'priority' are dropped silently
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should unknown or server-owned fields on create be rejected with 422, so client mistakes like a misspelled 'descripton' surface, or is silently dropping them intended?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: A misspelled optional field (for example 'descripton') is lost silently while the response reports success.

confirmedRules.name: Blocklist rejects everyday task wording through hyphens, globs, double dashes and the word 'or'
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Blocked keywords are matched as whole words, and any hyphen, slash or space counts as a word break; some symbols are blocked anywhere. As a result many ordinary ToDo titles and descriptions are rejected. The test suite treats blocking the English word 'or' as intended and allow-lists only one harmless phrase.
confirmedRules.given: A user enters a ToDo title on create or edit
confirmedRules.when: The title is 'Pick up drop-off slip', 'Re-create budget sheet', 'Tea or coffee?', 'Clean src/* folder', 'Gym Mon--Fri' or 'Eggs; milk'
confirmedRules.then: Each is rejected with 400 'Bad request'. 'Recreate budget sheet', 'Dropped off parcel', 'Ordered pizza', 'Updated CV' and "Don't forget" are accepted.
confirmedRules.parameters: Case-insensitive pattern blocking '--', ';', '/*', '*/' anywhere, plus the whole words xp_cmdshell, drop, delete, insert, update, exec, execute, union, select, shutdown, create, alter, rename, truncate, declare, or. Test data has 30 blocked patterns (including '1=1 OR 1=1' labelled 'OR keyword') and exactly 1 allowed phrase ('This was updated yesterday').
edgeCases: 'Re-create' and 'Pre-select' are blocked, while 'Recreate' and 'Preselect' are allowed
A cron expression such as '*/5' and a Markdown rule '---' are blocked
A keyword at the very start or end is blocked ('DROP this idea', 'Please DROP')
Full-width or look-alike Unicode letters (for example 'ＳＥＬＥＣＴ') are not matched
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is it acceptable that ordinary words such as 'or', 'update', 'create', 'select' and 'drop', and the symbols ';', '--' and '/*', are forbidden in ToDo text? Or should the rewrite rely on parameterized queries and drop the blocklist?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The blocklist adds no protection beyond the ORM's parameterized queries but rejects legitimate user text, and the test data checks only one harmless phrase, so false positives go untested.

confirmedRules.name: Input checks run before the 'not found' and 'already exists' checks (except when marking done)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If a request has bad input and also targets a todo that is missing, soft-deleted or already taken, the caller gets 'bad request' (400/422), not 'not found' (404) or 'already exists' (409). The one exception is marking done: it checks existence first and never validates the other fields.
confirmedRules.given: Todo A (id 7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7, title 'Pay rent') exists. Id M (0b1c2d3e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001) was never created, or was soft-deleted.
confirmedRules.when: (1) POST /todo {id: A, title: 'Drop off parcel'}; (2) POST /todo {id: A, title: '   '}; (3) POST /todo {id: A, title: 'Water plants'}; (4) PUT /todo/M {title: 'Select paint'}; (5) PUT /todo/M {title: 'Paint'}; (6) PUT /todo/M {title: 'Select paint', done: true}
confirmedRules.then: (1) 400 'Bad request': the blocked word 'drop' is caught before the duplicate id. (2) 422 schema error for the blank title. (3) 409 'ToDo already exists'. (4) 400 'Bad request', not 404. (5) 404 'ToDo not found'. (6) 404 'ToDo not found': existence is checked first and the title is never validated.
confirmedRules.parameters: Create check order: request schema (422) -> required-title and blocklist check in the builder (400) -> duplicate id at database commit (409). Edit without done=true: title, then description validation (400) -> lookup restricted to non-deleted todos (404). Edit with done=true: lookup only (404). Delete: path UUID (422) -> lookup (404).
edgeCases: An invalid edit to a soft-deleted todo returns 400, so the caller only learns the todo is gone after sending valid input
PUT /todo/M with {} or {'description': 'x'} returns 404 at once, because title validation only runs when a title is supplied
A duplicate id combined with a 256+ character title fails only at the database, and both errors map to 409, so they can't be told apart
The duplicate-id check happens only when the session commits on exiting the scope (database.py:54-64), after all business validation has passed
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Not wrong in itself, but undocumented. A rewrite that looks up the record (or checks for duplicates) before validating would return 404/409 where the legacy system returns 400, and contract tests would break.

confirmedRules.name: Completing a todo records no completion time (or deletion time)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Marking a todo done only flips the done flag. Nothing records when it was completed, reopened or deleted, so the roadmap's 'time to complete' analysis can't be computed from stored data.
confirmedRules.given: Todo 'Pay rent' was created on 2026-10-01 at 09:00 (created_at) with done=false
confirmedRules.when: PUT /todo/{id} {done: true} on 2026-10-03 at 18:30, then {done: false} on 2026-10-04, then {done: true} on 2026-10-05
confirmedRules.then: Each response shows the toggled done flag. The stored record has no completion date and no trace of the reopen, and updated_at keeps the value it got at insert. The first completion time (2 days 9.5 hours) can't be reconstructed.
confirmedRules.parameters: Fields written on mark-done: done=true plus a re-write of the current title and description. The toDo table has only id, title, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted and done. There is no completed_at, deleted_at or status-history column.
edgeCases: Reopening (done=false) erases all evidence that the todo was ever completed
Soft-deleting a done todo keeps done=true on the hidden row, but the deletion time isn't recorded anywhere
Legacy data can't be backfilled with real completion times after migration
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: README.md:115 plans time-to-complete tracking, but no completion timestamps are captured today, so pre-migration history can't support it.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the new system record completion (and deletion) timestamps or a status history? If so, how should legacy done todos be treated, given they have no completion date?

confirmedRules.name: The permanent-delete routine only works on active todos and can never purge soft-deleted ones
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The only routine that removes a todo row permanently first looks it up with the 'not deleted' filter. So it can only physically delete active todos, never ones already soft-deleted, which are exactly what a purge should remove.
confirmedRules.given: Todo A is active. Todo B was soft-deleted via DELETE /todo/{B} (deleted=true).
confirmedRules.when: hard_delete_to_do(A) and hard_delete_to_do(B) are called, for example by a future 'purge deleted todos' feature
confirmedRules.then: A's row is physically removed with no soft-delete step (returns true). B is reported as not found (returns false), and its row stays in the table.
confirmedRules.parameters: Lookup filter used before the physical delete: deleted IS FALSE (repository.py:88-89). Callers of hard_delete_to_do: none (the service delete uses only the soft delete_to_do at todo_service.py:72).
edgeCases: Unreachable today: no API endpoint, service method or scheduled job calls hard_delete_to_do
Wiring a purge feature to this method as-is would silently purge nothing and still look successful at the API level unless the false return is checked
Calling it on an active todo skips the soft-delete stage entirely, so the todo is unrecoverable at once
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The purge logic is inverted relative to the documented intent (README.md:108: permanently delete todos marked as deleted). It can delete only todos that are NOT marked deleted.

confirmedRules.name: The README roadmap's todo lifecycle differs from what the code implements
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The README lists soft delete, restore, a bulk 'purge all deleted' dialog and mark-as-done as future work. In code, soft delete and API mark-done/reopen already exist, while restore, bulk purge and any UI done control do not.
confirmedRules.given: README 'Further steps' lists: Deletion (mark as deleted, plus a dialog to permanently delete all todos marked deleted), Restore (undelete), Mark as done, Reminders (due dates) and Subtasks
confirmedRules.when: The rewrite team takes the todo lifecycle from the documentation instead of the code
confirmedRules.then: They would treat existing behaviour as new features and miss what's absent. What the code does: Active -> Deleted exists (DELETE /todo/{id}). Open <-> Done exists only via PUT done=true/false, with no UI control. Deleted -> Active (restore) doesn't exist. Deleted -> Purged doesn't exist; the only physical delete is per item, unused, and limited to active todos.
confirmedRules.parameters: Planned but not implemented: restore (README.md:109), bulk purge of all soft-deleted todos via a dialog (README.md:108), UI mark-as-done (README.md:110), due-date reminders (README.md:118), subtasks (README.md:117), time-to-complete tracking (README.md:115)
edgeCases: README.md:108 describes soft delete as future work, but repository.py:53-60 already implements it
README.md:110 describes mark-as-done as future work, but the API already supports it (todo_service.py:55-57); only the UI lacks it
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Which roadmap transitions belong in the target lifecycle? (a) Restore of soft-deleted todos: should it exist, and for how long after deletion? (b) Bulk purge of all soft-deleted todos: who may trigger it, and should there be an automatic retention period instead? (c) A UI control for done/reopen?

confirmedRules.name: The design doc's SUCCESS/FAILURE response status is not implemented
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The design document says every API response carries a status of SUCCESS or FAILURE. The code instead sends success=true on successes and only an error detail on failures, so FAILURE never appears.
confirmedRules.given: The design doc gives ToDoResponse, GetToDoResponse, ListToDoResponse and DeleteToDoResponse a field 'status: Status' (an enum of SUCCESS or FAILURE)
confirmedRules.when: A client calls GET /todo/{missing id}, or POST /todo with a valid new todo
confirmedRules.then: Missing id: HTTP 404 with body {detail: 'ToDo not found'}, with no status or success field. Valid create: HTTP 200 with {success: true, todo_entry: {...}, data: null, message: null, error: null}, with no status field.
confirmedRules.parameters: Implemented field: success (boolean, always true when present). Documented field: status enum SUCCESS/FAILURE. Unused envelope fields: data and error, always null. message is set only on delete ('Deleted successfully').
edgeCases: The success=false / FAILURE state can't be reached through any endpoint
Clients built from the design doc would look for a 'status' field that doesn't exist
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Documentation drift. The same file misspells created_at as 'reated_at' (backend.puml:31) and still marks the database package as 'Currently under reconstruction' (backend.puml:82).

confirmedRules.name: A rendering crash replaces the whole app with a 'Something went wrong' page that shows the raw error
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If the screen crashes while drawing, the header, list, form and notifications are all replaced by a 'Something went wrong' page showing the internal error message, plus a 'Try Again' button that re-draws the app without reloading the page.
confirmedRules.given: The app is showing the todo list
confirmedRules.when: A rendering error is thrown (for example, an unexpected value reaches a component) and the user then clicks 'Try Again'
confirmedRules.then: The app moves from Normal to Crashed: the full UI is replaced by 'Something went wrong' plus the error's message, or 'An unexpected error occurred' if there is none. 'Try Again' clears the crash state and re-renders. If the cause persists, the crash page returns at once.
confirmedRules.parameters: Fallback heading 'Something went wrong'; default message 'An unexpected error occurred'; button 'Try Again'. A custom fallback is supported but App doesn't use one.
edgeCases: Failed API calls don't trigger this state; they go to toasts or the list's own error screen with a Retry button (TodoList.tsx:13-24)
Raw internal error text is shown to end users
The boundary wraps everything, including the Chakra provider (App.tsx:14-16), yet its fallback uses Chakra components; whether the fallback renders correctly outside the provider wasn't verified

dataObjects.name: ToDoEntryData (domain entity / persistence record)

fields.name: id
fields.note: Primary key, supplied by the client. Normalised by UUIDValidator in the builder (todo_entry_builder.py:27). There is no server-side generation on the runtime path.

fields.name: title
fields.note: Checked against the blocklist and trimmed by FieldValidator.validate_required (todo_entry_builder.py:28; field_validator.py:29-35). Changed through setattr on update (repository.py:77-78).

fields.name: description
fields.note: On create, a missing or blank value becomes "" (field_validator.py:37-40). An explicit null on update is written as NULL (repository.py:77-78). The type annotation does not reflect the None case.

fields.name: created_at
fields.note: Set to datetime.datetime.now(): server-local and naive (todo_entry_builder.py:30). No code path changes it afterwards.

fields.name: updated_at
